model.name: Facility
model.purpose: Provide the governed, format-neutral context an agent needs to identify, classify, compose, operate, evidence and hand over a built facility as a managed aggregation of buildings, structures, systems and grounds.
model.scope_statement: A Facility is a bounded, operationally managed built entity that is planned, constructed, operated, maintained and eventually decommissioned as a unit under identified custody, and that aggregates one or more buildings, structures, engineered systems and associated grounds. The model covers the facility as (a) an identifiable real-world entity with registry standing, (b) an aggregation root over contained buildings and systems, and (c) an object of regulatory, financial, security and information governance. It deliberately excludes the internals of contained models (Building, Space, Equipment) and the land-tenure semantics of the containing Site.
in_scope: Facility identity, naming, reference designation and cross-registry keys
Functional, occupancy and code classification of the facility as an operating whole
Geospatial extent, georeference and jurisdictional location of the facility boundary
Containment by Site and decomposition into facility parts, buildings and structures
Facility-level engineered systems and linkage to the component asset register
Lifecycle phase, operational status, milestone events and record versioning
Condition, service life, deferred maintenance and criticality at facility level
Ownership, custody, legal interest, operator and facility-management accountability
Regulatory programme interests, permits, statutory inspections and nonconformities
Security level, protective posture and information disclosure constraints
Capacity, occupancy, utilisation and resource performance benchmarking
Asset information requirements, provenance, retention and standards alignment
out_of_scope: Land parcel tenure, cadastral boundaries and site acquisition (Site model WM-BLT-008)
Internal building fabric, storeys, structural systems and envelope (Building model WM-BLT-001)
Room and space geometry, occupancy assignment and wayfinding (Space model)
Component-level equipment records, serial numbers, warranties and spares (Equipment/Asset-item model)
Legal-entity attributes of owners, operators and regulators (Organization/Party model)
The permit or licence instrument itself, including its issuance workflow (Authorization model)
Postal address normalisation and address-point registry semantics (Address model)
Work-order execution, labour, scheduling and cost postings (Work Management model)
Financial valuation, depreciation and capital accounting (Financial Asset model)
Linear network topology of utilities and transport corridors beyond the facility boundary (Network/Utility model)
Individual person records, credentials and access-card issuance (Identity/Access model)
Construction project delivery, contracts and programme management (Project model)

boundary_notes.distinction: Site is the georeferenced land locus with tenure and parcel semantics; Facility is the operating unit placed on or spanning one or more sites. IFC keeps IfcSite and IfcFacility as distinct spatial structure elements and allows IfcFacility to be aggregated directly to IfcProject when no site information exists, so Site containment is normal but not universal.

Facility aggregates buildings and structures; Building holds fabric, storeys and envelope. This inverts the IFC type hierarchy, where IfcBuilding is a subtype of IfcFacility rather than its part. The registry CONTAINS relation is retained as an operational aggregation, and IFC subtyping is recorded as an alignment conflict rather than a conformance claim.

Facility stops at facility parts and building membership; interior spatial subdivision (IfcSpace, COBie Space and Zone, CityGML rooms) belongs to the Space model. Facility records only aggregate space counts and area totals.

Facility records facility-level systems and a pointer to the asset register with coverage and completeness measures; individual component identity, type data and maintenance history belong to the Equipment model (COBie Type and Component).

Facility references owner, custodian, demand organisation and service provider by identifier and role, with validity dates; it does not model legal-entity registration, corporate hierarchy or contracting capacity.

Facility carries regulatory programme interests, programme identifiers and permit references with validity windows; the permit instrument, its conditions text and issuance workflow belong to the Authorization model. EPA FRS models this as environmental interest types linked to a facility Registry ID.
Facility holds address references and administrative unit codes needed for reporting and emergency response; address parsing, normalisation and address-point authority belong to the Address model.

Facility is the object of management, not the management system. FM policy, objectives, competence and audit of the FM management system belong to a separate management-system model; Facility retains only the accountability links and service scope.

functions.name: Register facility
functions.description: Create a governed facility record with an authoritative identifier, minimal classification, containment and initial lifecycle state.
preconditions: Identity resolution has been run and no existing facility matches above the adjudication threshold
An issuing authority for the identifier scheme is named
Country and coordinate reference system are supplied
effects: A new persistent facility identifier is assigned and recorded as never-reusable
An append-only creation event is written with event time and ingestion time
Downstream registries are notified of the new identifier

functions.name: Resolve facility identity
functions.description: Match an inbound facility assertion against existing records using name, address, coordinates and programme identifiers, returning a match, a candidate set or a no-match decision with confidence.
outputs: matched facility identifier or candidate set
preconditions: Inbound assertion carries at least one location or identifier attribute
Match rules and thresholds are versioned and published
effects: An adjudication record is appended with the rule version and confidence
Below-threshold matches are queued for human adjudication rather than auto-merged
Merge or split decisions emit successor identifier links

functions.name: Classify facility
functions.description: Assign functional, reporting and code occupancy classifications to the facility in each adopted scheme, with precedence per downstream purpose.
inputs: authority having jurisdiction determination where applicable
preconditions: Primary function evidence is available
Each scheme version in use is declared
effects: Classification changes trigger review of permits, benchmarking baseline and occupancy determination
Prior classifications are retained with end dates rather than overwritten

functions.name: Assemble facility composition
functions.description: Bind the facility to its containing site, its facility parts, its member buildings and structures, and its engineered systems, applying an explicit decomposition convention.
preconditions: A decomposition convention has been selected and justified
Member references resolve to governed model instances
effects: Non-exclusive memberships are flagged and given an apportionment basis
Breakdown depth beyond the declared terminal level is rejected and routed to the Building or Space model

functions.name: Record lifecycle transition
functions.description: Record a change of lifecycle phase or operational status as an event with separate event, observation and ingestion times, and the evidence and authority behind it.
preconditions: The transition is permitted from the current state
Event time carries an explicit offset or Z
The asserting party holds authority for the transition
effects: Terminal transitions retain surviving regulatory and retention obligations
Handover into operation triggers the applicable information exchange requirements

functions.name: Assess condition and risk
functions.description: Record a condition assessment, service-life estimate, criticality rating and hazard exposure for the facility, attributable to a named method and assessor.
preconditions: Assessor competence is evidenced
Method version is declared and its scale is published
effects: Backlog above the escalation threshold raises a maintenance and investment finding
Criticality changes propagate to the security-level mission-criticality factor

functions.name: Verify regulatory standing
functions.description: Check that programme interests, permits, statutory inspections and certificates are current for the facility and surface expiries and open nonconformities.
preconditions: Programme interests are mapped to competent regulators
Permit validity windows are populated
effects: Expired or missing authorisations block publication of an operational status of in-use without an explicit exception
Overdue statutory inspections raise a compliance exception with an owner and deadline

functions.name: Publish facility performance
functions.description: Compute and publish capacity, utilisation and resource performance for a reporting period with declared boundary, normalisation, metered share and provenance.
preconditions: Metering boundary is declared relative to the facility extent
Gross floor area and operating hours are present and dated
effects: Restatements create a new report version citing the superseded one and notify downstream consumers
Estimated shares above the declared threshold mark the figures as advisory

functions.name: Apply disclosure controls
functions.description: Produce a release projection of the facility record with sensitivity markings applied, attributes withheld or generalised, exceptions honoured and access logged.
preconditions: Every scope carries a sensitivity marking
The requesting identity is authenticated and its role is resolved
effects: Withheld attributes are recorded as withheld with a legal basis rather than silently omitted
Geometry precision reduction is applied before any public release
An access log entry is written for restricted content

functions.name: Export facility exchange package
functions.description: Render the canonical facility payload and its artifacts into a chosen projection with crosswalk rows, integrity digests and the required bootstrap manifest.
preconditions: Record version has passed blocking validation rules
Target standard versions in the crosswalk are current
effects: Packages are immutable and integrity-verifiable
Lossy mappings are declared in the manifest rather than silently applied
No conformance is asserted without a cited evidence artifact

functions.name: Authorize or record occupancy
functions.description: Record a certificate of occupancy or equivalent AHJ authorization, including occupancy classification, code edition, occupant load and authorized portion.
preconditions: The object is a building or structure, or another facility type with a defined occupancy AHJ.
Change of occupancy is not asserted without a new authorization.
effects: Legal occupancy state is updated.
Unauthorized occupation remains prohibited in the model.

functions.name: Handover to operations
functions.description: Transfer relevant project information into the operational asset information model, mark the facility in-service after commissioning, and accept information containers in the CDE.
preconditions: Appointing party has specified operational information requirements.
Information containers have been checked against the level of information need.
effects: Operational phase information management is active.
Facility-in-service may be asserted if commissioning and handover are complete.

functions.name: Transfer ownership and AIM
functions.description: Record a change of owner or operator, run due diligence, transfer the AIM, and keep identity stable across the transaction.
preconditions: Incoming party is identified.
Security-minded handling is applied if required.
effects: Party-role history gains a new interval.
Information continuity is attempted; gaps are recorded rather than silently dropped.

composition.purpose: Bind the facility to its containing site or sites for georeference, tenure context and portfolio rollup, while leaving parcel and land-tenure semantics in the Site model. Modelled as conditional because a facility may be the outermost spatial container.
Aggregate the buildings and structures that constitute the facility, with membership validity and exclusivity, delegating fabric, storeys and envelope to the Building model.
Reference interior spaces and zones for area totals, service relationships and occupancy without duplicating space geometry or assignment.
Link the facility to component-level asset records via a declared linkage key, with register coverage and inventory recency held here and item detail held there.
Resolve owner, custodian, demand organisation, service provider, regulator and assessor roles to governed party identifiers with validity windows.
Attach permits, licences and programme authorisations to the facility by reference, keeping instrument text, conditions and issuance workflow in the Authorization model.
Resolve role-tagged addresses and administrative units without embedding address parsing or address-point authority.
Resolve work orders, jobs and resources back to facility and system so that maintenance backlog and history are computable without duplicating execution records.
Supply the common pattern of value, unit, method, observation time and ingestion time used by condition, area, occupancy and resource-performance findings.
Supply record validity bounds, real-world validity, change kind and supersession semantics applied uniformly across facility findings.

Align facility identity, composition and placement with the IFC spatial structure. Alignment only: IFC subordinates IfcBuilding to IfcFacility by subtyping, whereas this model aggregates buildings under a facility.
Align geometry, level of detail and city-object versioning for geospatial exchange and digital-twin use, independent of GML or any other encoding.
Align facility handover content with the Facility, Level, Space, Zone, Type, Component, System, Job and Document tables so construction-to-operations exchange is lossless in the covered subset.
Align persistent identifiers, lifespan versioning and construction-condition semantics for European geospatial publication.

Align to linked-data building vocabularies for graph projection. Recorded as partial: neither vocabulary offers a facility class between site and building, so facility identity must be carried by an extension term.
Align the facility asset register, criticality, life-cycle decision-making and documented-information requirements with the asset management system that governs the portfolio.
Align information requirements, trigger events and asset information model acceptance with the operational-phase information management process.

owner_package_requirements: A Dimension adopting WM-BLT-006 must name a single accountable facility or infrastructure owner-operator package and a named data steward role before any facility record is published.

The owner package must declare its identifier scheme, issuing authority and non-reuse policy, and must state which external registry (for example an environmental facility registry or a real-property inventory) it treats as the authoritative master for identity.

The owner package must publish its adopted code lists and versions for lifecycle phase, operational status, legal interest, classification schemes and sensitivity markings, and must version them independently of the model.
The owner package must define the terminal decomposition level at which responsibility passes to the Building, Space and Equipment models, and must reject deeper structure at validation time.
The owner package must nominate the retention schedule authority applicable in its jurisdiction and map every artifact class in this model to a schedule item.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a stable, resolvable namespace under the adopting Dimension, segmented by record plane and model, for example {dimension-root}/world-model/wm-blt-006/{facility-identifier}. Node identifiers within the model are lower-kebab-case and stable for the life of the model; renaming a node requires a new identifier plus an explicit supersession link. External identifiers keep their issuing authority's namespace and are never rewritten into the local namespace. Where linked-data projection is used, mint facility IRIs in the Dimension namespace and relate them to external vocabularies by alignment properties rather than by asserting equivalence.
registry_links: vr.wm-blt-006 is the registry entry of record for this model; nav path NAV.PHY.BLT.FAC and domain tags PHY.BLT.FAC are the authoritative navigation keys.

Relation edges to WM-BLT-008 (Site contains Facility) and WM-BLT-001 (Facility contains Building) are maintained in planning/VERCY-MODEL-RELATIONS.csv and must be updated in the same change as any composition change here.

Sibling models referenced but not owned (Organization, Address, Authorization, Equipment, Space, Work Management) must be registered before a Dimension may assert the corresponding REFERENCE links as required.

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is the logical payload defined by this model, not any serialisation. JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections and must round-trip the canonical payload without semantic loss.
Property order is not semantic; canonical comparison sorts object members by identifier and orders collections by their declared natural key, falling back to identifier then observation time.

All time values are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; no local-time-without-offset values are canonical, and dates that are genuinely partial use the declared partial-date structure rather than a padded timestamp.
Quantities are canonical only with an explicit unit and, where applicable, a measurement method and standard reference; bare numbers for area, energy and monetary values are rejected.
Geometry is canonical only with an explicit coordinate reference system and, where vertical values are present, a vertical datum.
Empty, null and absent are distinct: absent means not asserted, null means asserted as unknown, and a withheld marker means asserted but not disclosed.
patch_rules: Patches are expressed as ordered operations against canonical paths and must declare whether each operation is a real-world change or a correction of a prior error.
Every patch carries the base record version it applies to; a patch against a superseded version is rejected rather than rebased automatically.

Patches never mutate append-only artifacts (event log, version history, provenance report, disposition register, exchange packages); corrections to those are appended as new entries citing the corrected sequence.
Identifier fields are not patchable. Changing identity requires a merge or split event that emits successor links and preserves both prior identifiers as non-reusable.
A patch that would change classification, occupancy group, legal interest, security level or sensitivity marking requires the authority named for that finding and is rejected without it.
Patches must pass all blocking validation rules before commit; advisory rule failures are recorded on the resulting version rather than blocking it.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional finding, question, data element or artifact is a minor change. Removing one, tightening cardinality, making an element required, or narrowing a code list is a breaking change.

Code list values may be added in a minor change; retiring a value requires deprecation with an end date and a documented successor value, and existing records retain the retired value with their original validity.
External standard alignments are versioned independently of the model; a target standard revision creates a new crosswalk row and never edits an existing one.
Consumers must ignore unknown members in a projection rather than fail, but must not infer meaning for members absent from the canonical payload.
No conformance to an external standard is claimed at any version without a cited evidence artifact; alignment claims are the default and must be labelled as such.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the facility, such as a real-property inventory unique identifier or an environmental facility registry identifier.
Governed global identifier or IRI issued by a recognised registry or minted in the adopting Dimension's resolvable namespace under a published minting policy.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only when neither of the above exists, and recorded together with the reason no governed identifier was available.

A date, a name, an address, a coordinate pair and a reference designation are never identifiers. Reference designations under ISO 81346-12 denote positions in an aspect structure and expressly exclude serial and inventory numbering.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All timestamps are RFC 3339 with seconds precision and an explicit numeric UTC offset or Z. Event time, observation time and ingestion time are recorded as separate fields wherever they can differ, and a value asserted with only one of them must declare which one it is.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named {facility-identifier}--{artifact-id}--{zero-padded-sequence}--{RFC-3339-creation-timestamp}. Sequences are monotonic per facility and artifact class, never reused, and gaps must be explained by a recorded void entry rather than silently closed.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a named digest algorithm and digest value in its package manifest. Immutable artifacts (event logs, version histories, assessments once approved, issued certificates, exchange packages) are verified on read and on export; a digest mismatch blocks use and raises a provenance exception rather than being repaired in place. Artifacts are referenced from records by identifier plus digest, never by mutable path alone.

policies: Alignment is the default relationship to any external standard. Conformance is asserted only where a cited evidence artifact from a test suite or accredited assessment exists, and the claim carries the exact target version.

Identity is never inferred from name, address or coordinates alone. Automated matching below the published adjudication threshold produces a candidate set for human decision, and every merge or split is an auditable event with successor links.

No facility attribute is published without its provenance: source system, observation time and ingestion time. Values that are estimated, derived or matched carry a confidence measure and are labelled as such in every projection.

Sensitivity marking is mandatory at bundle, layer, finding and artifact scope. Withheld attributes are disclosed as withheld with a legal basis; silent omission is prohibited because it is indistinguishable from absence of data.

Retention is scheduled per record class against a named jurisdictional authority. Destruction requires authorisation and leaves an auditable destruction record; records eligible for archival transfer are offered before any disposition is applied.

Boundary discipline is enforced: a change that would add parcel tenure, building fabric, room geometry, component detail or party registration data to this model is rejected and routed to the owning sibling model.
Do not treat a certificate of occupancy as exhausting fire-code, environmental-program or information-security duties.
Do not merge facility records solely on similar names or ZIP-centroid coordinates.
Do not classify a single equipment asset or an unbuilt nature preserve as a facility.
Apply security-minded handling to location, occupancy, risk and system fields of high-security facilities.
Keep Site, Building, Asset, Party and Infrastructure in sibling models; reference them with typed edges.

read: Read is scoped by sensitivity marking at bundle, layer, finding and artifact level; a reader receives a projection with withheld markers rather than a silently reduced record.
Historic reads are answerable as-of a record version time and as-of a real-world date, and the two must be requestable independently.
Reads of restricted content are logged with subject identity, scope, purpose and RFC 3339 timestamp.
Public projections apply geometry precision reduction and the published redaction rule set before release.
create: Creation requires a resolved identity decision, a named issuing authority for the identifier, country and coordinate reference system, lifecycle phase, operational status and a sensitivity marking.
Creation is refused where identity resolution returns a match above the adjudication threshold; the caller must instead amend the existing facility or raise a split decision.
Creation writes version 1 plus a creation event carrying event time, ingestion time and the asserting party.
update: Updates are versioned, never destructive. Each new version declares change kind (real-world change or correction) and cites the version it supersedes.
Updates to classification, occupancy group, legal interest, security level or sensitivity marking require the authority named in the corresponding finding.
Updates that fail a blocking validation rule are rejected with the failing rule identifiers; advisory failures are attached to the resulting version.
Bulk updates from a source system are applied under the published precedence rules and never overwrite a higher-precedence value.
delete: Facility records are not deleted while any retention obligation or surviving regulatory obligation is open; decommissioning is a lifecycle transition, not a deletion.
Logical deletion sets an end of real-world validity and an end of record validity, retaining the identifier as permanently non-reusable.

Physical destruction occurs only under an authorised disposition action, is evidenced by a destruction record, and retains the minimum tombstone metadata (identifier, record class, schedule item, disposition date, authorising role).
Deletion requests that would break a referenced edge from a sibling model are refused until the referencing model has been updated.

roles.name: Facility owner-operator (accountable owner)
responsibilities: Owns the model instance for a given facility and accepts accountability for its accuracy and completeness.
Approves lifecycle transitions, legal interest changes and disposal decisions.
Nominates the data steward and the named accountable persons for statutory duties.

roles.name: Facility data steward
responsibilities: Maintains identifier assignment, cross-registry references and the deduplication adjudication queue.
Publishes and versions code lists, validation rules, match thresholds and source precedence.
Runs periodic reconciliation against external registries and records unresolved conflicts.

roles.name: Information manager
responsibilities: Maintains organisational, asset and exchange information requirements and the trigger-event calendar.
Accepts or rejects information deliverables into the asset information model and records the decision.
Owns the canonical payload definition, crosswalk matrix and exchange packaging rules.

roles.name: Compliance and records officer
responsibilities: Maintains programme interests, permits, statutory inspection schedules and open nonconformities.
Maps every artifact class to a retention schedule item and executes authorised dispositions with evidence.
Escalates expired authorisations and overdue statutory inspections to the accountable owner.

roles.name: Security and disclosure authority
responsibilities: Determines and reviews the facility security level and required protective measures.
Assigns sensitivity markings at bundle, layer, finding and artifact scope and approves redaction rules.
Grants, time-bounds and reviews access exceptions, and reviews the access audit log.

roles.name: Consuming agent (automated)
responsibilities: Reads AGENTS.md before any other file and follows the declared read order.
Treats absent, null and withheld as distinct and never infers values for withheld or absent attributes.
Refuses to assert conformance, identity matches or performance figures without the accompanying provenance and evidence references.

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Access is granted per scope (bundle, layer, finding, artifact) to an authenticated identity holding a role explicitly bound to that scope's sensitivity marking, for a declared purpose. Facility information is not presumed public: statutory real-property publication regimes expressly authorise excluding assets for national-security reasons and under freedom-of-information exemptions, so the model treats openness as a per-scope decision rather than a default.
exceptions: Emergency response: the emergency-response address, representative point, occupant population, hazard classification and utility demarcation points are released to a recognised emergency service on assertion of an incident, with post-hoc logging rather than prior approval.

Statutory disclosure: regulatory programme interests, permit references and required environmental or energy disclosures are released to the competent regulator regardless of internal marking, limited to the attributes the obligation names.

Security-restricted attributes: security level determination, countermeasure status, detailed floor geometry and critical-system demarcation are withheld from public projections and released only under a time-bounded exception granted by the security and disclosure authority.

National-security and freedom-of-information exclusions: whole facilities may be excluded from public inventory publication, in which case the exclusion itself and its legal basis are recorded even though the record is not released.

Research and benchmarking: aggregate or generalised projections (coarsened geometry, banded areas, banded occupancy) may be released where the release cannot re-identify a restricted facility, subject to a documented re-identification assessment.
High-security and high-security-zone facilities may omit or coarsen address and coordinates.
Personal contact data in affiliations is privacy-restricted.
Alleged compliance status must be labelled as alleged where not adjudicated.
Indian-country and similar jurisdictional flags are visible to authorized program roles and may be restricted in public projections.
audit_requirements: Log every read, export and share of restricted-marked content with subject identity, scope reference, declared purpose, projection produced and RFC 3339 timestamp.
Log every access-exception grant with granting role, justification, scope, expiry timestamp and the revocation or expiry event.
Log every merge, split, identifier assignment and sensitivity-marking change as an immutable event with the asserting party.
Log every disposition action with the schedule item, authorising role and destruction or transfer evidence reference.
Retain audit logs at least as long as the longest retention obligation applying to the facility record classes they cover, and verify their integrity digests on read.
Record who read or changed security-minded, identity-merge, occupancy-authorization and owner-transfer fields, with event time and ingestion time.
Steward merge and split decisions are immutable audit artifacts.

required_fields: Canonical payload and canonicalization rules URL
Sensitivity marking and access policy URL
Crosswalk matrix URL and conformance claim status
read_order: AGENTS.md — read first and in full before any other artifact, including when the store is a database or an MCP server rather than a file tree.
Specification URL — the model definition, bundle and layer structure, findings and required data elements.
Storage type URL — how the canonical payload is projected into the actual store, and which projection-specific constraints apply.
Interface URL — the read, create, update and delete operations exposed, their scopes and their authentication requirements.
Processes URL — the governed functions, their preconditions and effects, and the approval authorities for restricted transitions.
Sensitivity marking and access policy — before requesting or rendering any facility attribute.
Crosswalk matrix and conformance claim status — before mapping content into or out of any external standard.

coverage.claim: Merged model covers the context an agent needs to identify, classify, compose, operate, evidence, govern and exchange a built facility as an operationally managed aggregate, using the Claude result as base (explicit in/out-of-scope lists keyed to named sibling models, eight sourced boundary notes, bitemporal and retention discipline) plus five Grok findings for facility eligibility and non-building/mobile cases, AHJ occupancy authorization, alleged-versus-adjudicated compliance status, facility-scale fire and life safety, and post-occupancy evaluation. Bounded to the facility aggregate only: Site, Building, Space, Equipment, Organization, Authorization, Address and Work Management remain sibling models. No claim of universal, cross-jurisdiction or metaphysical completeness is made; code lists remain Dimension-declared.

checklist.notes: Master-system key, governed external registry identifiers, non-reuse, merge and split, and match confidence are grounded in the EPA Facility Site Identification Data Standard, the FRS registry pattern and INSPIRE persistent-identifier rules. Reference designations are explicitly excluded from identity because ISO 81346-12 excludes serial and inventory numbering from its scope.

Phase set from ISO 15686-1, operational status from real-property inventory and INSPIRE construction-condition semantics, handover and trigger events from ISO 19650-3, terminal states with surviving obligations. Gap: no primary source consulted supplies a single normative facility status code list, so the model requires the adopting Dimension to declare and version its own.

Site containment (conditional, because IFC allows a facility as outermost container), facility part decomposition with a mandatory usage convention, building membership with validity and exclusivity, system-to-space service edges, and typed references to seven sibling models.

Bitemporal discipline with record validity bounds, real-world validity, event time, observation time and ingestion time; RFC 3339 with explicit offset mandated; partial dates handled by a declared structure rather than padding; correction versus real-world change distinguished explicitly.

Per-attribute source system, precedence ranking, match confidence, estimated versus metered shares and restatement handling, modelled on the federated-registry integration and best-pick pattern and on benchmarking data-quality practice.

Legal interest, title holder, custodial control and encumbrances separated from operating accountability; the demand-organisation to service-provider distinction is taken from ISO 41011 facility-management vocabulary.

Blocking versus advisory rules, publication gate, canonical-form constraints (unit required, CRS required, offset required), reconciliation tolerances for apportioned area, and deduplication adjudication thresholds.

Deny-by-default with per-scope sensitivity markings across bundle, layer, finding and artifact; five named exception classes including emergency response and statutory disclosure; audit obligations. Grounded in the statutory authority to exclude federal real property from publication for national-security and FOIA-exemption reasons, and in the ISC security-level standard.

Record classes mapped to schedule items with trigger, period and disposition action; decommissioning modelled as a lifecycle transition rather than deletion; tombstone metadata preserved; archival-offer obligation before disposition. Grounded in NARA GRS 5.4 (Transmittal 35, May 2024).

Alignments to IFC 4.3, CityGML 3.0, COBie V3, INSPIRE Buildings, SAREF4BLDG, BOT, ISO 55001 and ISO 19650-3, each versioned, direction-tagged and lossiness-flagged, with conformance withheld absent cited evidence.

Functional and reporting classification with per-purpose precedence, plus legally consequential code occupancy classification asserted by an authority having jurisdiction. Uniclass Complexes versus Entities is recorded as a granularity decision rather than a fixed mapping.
Representative point, extent geometry, CRS and vertical datum, accuracy, level of detail, relative versus absolute placement, addressing roles and jurisdictional straddling.

Area under a declared measurement standard, capacity, occupancy, utilisation formula, resource metrics with normalisation and benchmark reference, metering boundary declaration and metered-versus-estimated share.

Security level determination factors, five-level scale, required versus implemented countermeasures with approved deviations, critical-infrastructure designation and reassessment cadence, from the ISC Risk Management Process 2021 Edition.

Criticality and mission dependency with declared method, hazard exposure with likelihood and severity basis, redundancy and recovery objectives, exercise evidence. Gap: no consulted primary source defines a cross-sector criticality scale, so the method must be named by the adopting Dimension.
Programme interests with regulator and programme identifier, permits with validity and conditions, statutory inspections with due dates, open nonconformities with corrective actions and deadlines.

Valuation, depreciation, capital accounting and cost postings are routed to a Financial Asset model. Only deferred maintenance liability is retained here, because condition reporting requires it and real-property inventory guidance reports it alongside condition.

Occupant population is modelled only as aggregate counts by category. Person-level occupancy, access-credential records and workplace monitoring raise data-protection duties that no consulted source addresses at facility level; these are deferred to an Identity/Access model and flagged as an evidence gap rather than covered here.

known_omissions: ISO 55001:2024, ISO 41011:2024, ISO 19650-3:2020, ISO 81346-12:2018 and ISO 15686-1:2011 are paywalled. Their scope, structure and key distinctions were taken from the ISO catalogue records and committee material; exact normative clause text and full term definitions were not read, so no clause-level conformance is asserted anywhere in this model.

The FY2026 FRPP Data Dictionary PDF could not be machine-parsed during research. It is cited for the existence and authority of the reporting data elements (identifier, asset type, legal interest, status, size, condition, mission dependency, utilisation, disposition), not for verbatim element names or code values.

The EPA Facility Site Identification Data Standard PDF could not be machine-parsed. Its data groupings are cited at the level confirmed by EPA's own summary pages; individual element names and formats should be re-verified against the PDF before implementation.

No consulted source provides a normative, cross-jurisdiction code list for facility operational status, criticality scale or maintenance strategy. These are marked as Dimension-declared code lists rather than presented as canonical.

Sustainability and green-building certification (LEED, BREEAM, energy performance certificates under the EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive) is not modelled as a separate finding; only benchmarked resource performance is covered. This was rejected as attractive but insufficiently grounded at facility rather than building level in the sources consulted.
Insurance, valuation and loss-history context is absent. It is genuinely part of the facility decision surface but no primary source in the consulted set supports a defensible structure for it.

Digital-twin runtime telemetry, building automation point naming (for example Brick or Project Haystack) and control-system topology are not modelled; only the static system register and reference designation are covered.

Marine, rail, road and bridge facility specialisations are acknowledged through IFC subtypes but not elaborated. A facility with no buildings at all is supported structurally but its domain-specific context is out of scope.
ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and other energy-benchmarking facility IDs were not fetched as primary sources.
Uniclass, OmniClass, MasterFormat and similar construction classification tables are not included.
CISA critical-infrastructure sector designations lack primary support here.
NFPA 101/25/72, ASME A17.1 and equivalent ongoing inspection regimes are not specified beyond the note that a CO does not satisfy them.
COBie as a distinct handover schema is not specified; ISO 19650 AIM is used instead.
ISO 21542 / ADA accessibility beyond IFC HandicapAccessible is not specified.
Climate-risk scoring, whole-life cost models and GHG inventories are vocabulary-aligned in ISO 41011 but not operationalized as findings.
Temporary event facilities, underground mines, nuclear licensed sites and vessels as facilities are not developed.
National facility registers outside the US EPA FRS (for example European PRTR or other cadastres) are not included.
ISO 19650-5 is cited via ISO 19650-3 but was not fetched as a primary document.
conflicts: IFC 4.3 makes IfcBuilding a subtype of IfcFacility, whereas the registry relation and this model make Facility an aggregate that contains Building (WM-BLT-001). These are incompatible readings of the same word: IFC says a building is a kind of facility, this model says a facility is a set of buildings. Recorded as an alignment conflict; the crosswalk must map a single-building facility to IfcBuilding directly rather than to IfcFacility plus a child.

The W3C Building Topology Ontology exposes bot:Site with bot:hasBuilding and provides no class between site and building. Any BOT projection of a multi-building facility must introduce an extension term or collapse the facility, losing the aggregation. Alignment is therefore declared partial and lossy.

EPA FRS models a 'facility site' scoped to regulatory interest. A regulated facility site can be co-extensive with, larger than, or smaller than a Vercy Facility, and can be co-extensive with a Site. The site-contains-facility containment therefore cannot be assumed when reconciling with environmental registries.

ENERGY STAR treats a multi-building campus as a parent 'property' with child buildings, using property and property-use terminology that does not map cleanly onto site, facility and building. The parent property may correspond to a Facility or to a Site depending on how the portfolio was set up.

Uniclass places Complexes (Co) above Entities (En), so a Vercy Facility may classify as a complex or as an entity depending on granularity. No rule in the consulted sources determines which, so the choice is left to the adopting Dimension and must be recorded.

ISO 41011 facility-management vocabulary uses 'facility' more broadly than the built-asset scope adopted here, including service and non-built assets. This model narrows the term deliberately and records the narrowing rather than claiming vocabulary conformance.

IFC allows a facility to be aggregated directly to a project with no site, contradicting any modelling that makes Site containment mandatory. The composition link to WM-BLT-008 is therefore marked not required.
IFC 4.3 treats IfcBuilding as a subtype of IfcFacility; this model treats Facility as containing Building. Alignment only; no IFC conformance claim.
EPA FIDS/FRS treats a facility as a distinct real-property facility-site and often conflates land and operations; ISO/IFC distinguish Site from Facility.
FHIR Location ranges from bed and freezer to building and mobile clinic; using it as the Facility aggregate would over-cover spaces and kinds.
ISO 19650-3 uses asset as a convenience term covering asset management and facility management; ISO 41011 keeps facility distinct from asset.
IBC occupancy authorization applies to buildings and structures, not necessarily to roads, railways or other civil IfcFacility subtypes.
Facility names and addresses routinely differ across EPA program systems after ownership change; name matching without steward review is unsafe.
ECHO compliance status is often alleged tracking status, not adjudication.
regional_assumptions: The FRPP data dictionary, FRS and the Facility Site Identification Data Standard, NARA GRS 5.4, the ISC Risk Management Process, the International Building Code and ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager are United States instruments. Adopters elsewhere must substitute equivalent national real-property inventories, environmental registries, retention schedules, protective-security standards, building codes and benchmarking regimes; the structural findings are intended to survive that substitution but the code lists are not.

The INSPIRE Buildings data specification and its identifier and lifespan rules are European Union instruments implementing Commission Regulation (EU) No 1089/2010 and apply only where INSPIRE publication obligations exist.

Uniclass is a United Kingdom classification. Adopters in other regions will more likely use OmniClass, a national equivalent or an industry activity classification, and the crosswalk must record which.

Coordinate reference systems, vertical datums, address structures and administrative unit hierarchies are region-specific. The model mandates that CRS and datum be declared but does not prescribe values.

Data-protection duties over occupancy and access data vary substantially by jurisdiction. The model deliberately holds only aggregate occupancy and defers person-level data, but adopters in strict-regime jurisdictions should verify that even aggregate occupancy counts are lawful to retain and publish.

Retention periods differ sharply between public-sector schedules and private-sector obligations. The three-year default reflected in the cited government-wide schedule must not be generalised; adopters must map to their own scheduling authority.
EPA FRS, NAICS/SIC, Indian-country and federal-facility indicators are United States environmental-program constructs.
IBC 2021 Section 111 is a US model code; adopting jurisdictions may use other editions or national building codes with different occupancy certificates.
FHIR Location is healthcare-centric and is an optional alignment for hospitals and clinics, not a general facility register.
IFC GlobalId is an exchange-world identifier, not a legal or environmental master ID.
Best-pick NAD83 coordinates and ZIP-centroid approximations are US FRS/ECHO behaviours.
Land-title numbers on IfcSite follow local cadastral practice and are references, not a world land register.
adversarial_checks: Counterexample: a road, railway, bridge or marine facility that contains no buildings at all. IFC treats these as first-class facility subtypes. The model survives because building membership is optional and decomposition uses an explicit usage convention, but the registry's 'Facility contains buildings or structures' rationale is only conditionally true and is recorded as such.

Counterexample: a single-building facility where Facility and Building are co-extensive. This risks duplicating WM-BLT-001. Resolved by requiring the terminal decomposition level to be declared and by mapping such cases directly to IfcBuilding in the crosswalk rather than creating a facility node plus a redundant child.

Counterexample: leased floors inside a third-party multi-tenant building operated as a facility by a tenant. Here the facility is smaller than the building, inverting the containment. The model accommodates this through non-exclusive membership with an apportionment basis and a legal interest of leased, but the CONTAINS edge to WM-BLT-001 is semantically strained and is flagged for review.

Counterexample: a facility spanning several parcels, two municipalities and two utility service territories. Tests exclusive site containment and single-jurisdiction assumptions; addressed by the straddling question, multi-site references and apportionment rules, but no consulted source prescribes an apportionment method, so this remains a Dimension decision.

Counterexample: a mothballed or disposed facility that still carries environmental permits, monitoring obligations and long-lived record retention. Tests whether terminal lifecycle states terminate obligations; the model explicitly separates operational status from surviving obligations and blocks deletion while any obligation is open.

Counterexample: a facility whose public record is lawfully withheld in its entirety for national-security reasons. Tests whether absence and withholding are distinguishable; the model requires the exclusion and its legal basis to be recorded even when the record is not released, so a consumer can tell 'withheld' from 'does not exist'.
Rejected structure: a dedicated Address bundle. Rejected as duplicating a sibling Address model; only role-tagged references and jurisdictional placement are retained.

Rejected structure: a Sustainability Certification bundle. Rejected because the consulted primary sources support benchmarking metrics at property level but do not support a defensible certification structure at facility level; folded into resource performance and recorded as a known omission.

Rejected structure: an Occupant bundle holding person-level occupancy. Rejected on privacy grounds and for lack of primary support at facility level; deferred to an Identity/Access model and recorded as an explicit coverage gap rather than silently dropped.
Could Facility collapse into Site? Only if EPA facility-site conflation is adopted; ISO 41011 and IFC IfcSite versus IfcFacility keep them distinct, so collapse is rejected and recorded as conflict.
Could Facility collapse into Building? Only if IFC subtype is adopted; Vercy known relation and ISO 41011 collection-of-assets definition keep Building as a contained shelter object.
Is a car, AHU or nature preserve a facility? ISO/TR 41013 says no; the eligibility function rejects those candidates.
Can a facility exist with no site and no building? IFC allows direct assignment to project and non-building subtypes; the model allows it.
Can one facility span many sites? Unresolved; agents must record multi-site as a boundary note rather than invent a universal rule.
Does a certificate of occupancy end regulatory duty? No; IBC authorizes occupancy while environmental and fire-code programs may continue, including after operations cease.
Is FM or ISO 41001 the same object as Facility? No; FM is the organizational function and management system; Facility is the asset collection those functions operate.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently reached entry_kind=aggregate for vr.wm-blt-006, and both independently rejected the two collapse candidates: Facility into Site (rejected because ISO 41011 and IfcSite/IfcFacility keep land locus distinct from operating asset collection) and Facility into Building (rejected because IFC 4.3 subtyping is recorded as an alignment conflict, not adopted as the registry relation). The registry CONTAINS edge to WM-BLT-001 is retained as operational aggregation; Site containment is retained as conditional because IFC permits a facility aggregated directly to a project with no site. No split, reclassification or merge is warranted: the boundary between the Facility aggregate and the Facility Management management system (ISO 41001) is stated identically by both providers.

decisions.rationale: Claude states twelve in-scope and twelve out-of-scope items each keyed to a named sibling model, gives eight source-referenced boundary notes, and carries the governance spine the merged model needs (bitemporal versioning, retention and disposition, disclosure control, crosswalk lossiness). Grok's bundle set is wider but its boundaries repeat inside findings rather than being declared once; size was not the deciding factor.

Independent agreement between providers, and both reached it by rejecting the same two collapse candidates (into Site and into Building) with the same primary evidence, which is stronger than mere agreement on a label.

decisions.concept: Facility CONTAINS Building versus IFC 4.3 IfcBuilding-as-subtype
decisions.disposition: Retained as recorded alignment conflict; registry CONTAINS relation kept
decisions.rationale: Both providers independently declined IFC conformance and recorded the inversion. Base additionally prescribes that a single-building facility maps directly to IfcBuilding in the crosswalk rather than to IfcFacility plus a redundant child, which resolves the practical case without changing the boundary.

decisions.disposition: Conditional edge to WM-BLT-008, not mandatory
decisions.rationale: IFC permits a facility aggregated directly to a project with no site, and both providers reached this conclusion separately. The composition link must therefore be marked not-required rather than assumed.

Base only carried this reasoning in adversarial checks; a registered agent needs a first-class test that rejects a single asset, an unbuilt asset, a kind-of-location classifier, or a room, and admits civil and mobile facilities.

decisions.concept: Certificate of occupancy as authorization gate
decisions.disposition: Accepted from grok, bounded to reference plus scope and validity
decisions.rationale: Distinct from occupancy classification, which the base already holds. The instrument's issuance workflow and conditions text stay in the Authorization sibling model per the base out-of-scope list, so the addition does not breach the declared boundary.

Base tracks open nonconformities but not the legal weight of a reported determination or its refresh lag. Misreporting alleged as adjudicated is a concrete downstream harm and the ECHO data dictionary supports the distinction directly.

Base risk coverage is exposure and continuity plus protective security; fire risk, sprinkler and exit provisions and emergency preparedness were genuinely absent. Accepted with the source's own caveat that detailed life-safety design belongs to Building and Space models.

decisions.disposition: Accepted from grok, service-life portion suppressed
decisions.rationale: POE is defined in ISO 41011 and placed on the ISO 19650-3 operational timeline and is missing from the base. Service life remains mastered by the base condition-and-service-life finding to avoid two masters for the same measure.

decisions.concept: Grok identifier, naming, address and coordinate findings
decisions.rationale: Base already covers master key and external registry precedence, non-reuse, merge and split, alias validity, address roles and jurisdiction, CRS, vertical datum, accuracy, level of detail and relative-versus-absolute placement. Adding these would create parallel structure without new decision surface.

decisions.concept: Grok identity-matching-and-data-quality (no silent merge without steward review)
decisions.disposition: Rejected as a finding; retained as a required answer under the base deduplication question
decisions.rationale: Base already asks what deduplication and match-confidence rule applies and what confidence accompanies matched values. The steward-adjudication control is the answer to those questions, not a separate structure, and duplicating it would split match governance across two layers.

Base operator-and-service-accountability already carries delegated service scope, governing agreement and what the demand organisation retains, and both providers put SLA commercial terms and the FM management system out of scope. Only mobilization state was novel, which is insufficient for a finding.

decisions.disposition: Deferred to the crosswalk matrix, not adopted as structure
decisions.rationale: FHIR Location spans beds, freezers, vehicles and buildings, so adopting it as the facility aggregate would over-cover spaces and kinds; grok itself records this as a conflict. It may be added as a versioned alignment row under the base crosswalk finding once a healthcare profile is validated.

decisions.disposition: Not adopted as bundles; accepted content routed into existing base layers
decisions.rationale: Base already places ownership, custody and operating accountability under authority-tenure-and-compliance and security posture under the same bundle. Creating parallel bundles would fragment authority semantics; the two accepted safety and authorization findings fit existing layers cleanly.

publicationHolds: Source and live-version verification is incomplete: the same EPA Facility Site Identification Data Standard PDF is dated 2014-10-01 Version 2 by claude (SRC-004) and 2006-01-06 Version 2.0 by grok (SRC-003), and the two providers assign it different authority tiers. Re-fetch and pin one date, version and tier before any citation is published.

Pin a single IFC documentation reference: claude cites the ifc43-docs build 4.3.2.20260821 (IFC4X3_ADD2) while grok cites standards.buildingsmart.org IFC 4.3.2.0 mapped to ISO 16739-1:2024. Both URLs must be re-resolved live and one canonical citation chosen for IfcFacility, IfcFacilityPart and IfcSite.

All ISO sources on both sides (41011, 6707-4, 19650-3, 55001, 81346-12, 15686-1) were taken from catalogue or Online Browsing Platform records, not normative clause text. Hold any clause-level or conformance wording; publish alignment language only, and state the non-reading explicitly in the draft.

Claude records that the FY2026 FRPP Data Dictionary and the EPA FIDS PDF could not be machine-parsed, so element names, formats and code values are unverified. Publish these as existence-and-authority citations only; block implementation-level field naming until re-parsed.

Multi-profile domain validation is not complete. The merged evidence is dominated by US federal instruments (FRS, FRPP, NARA GRS 5.4, ISC, IBC, ENERGY STAR, ECHO) plus EU INSPIRE and one healthcare alignment. Validate against at least one non-US built-asset profile and one non-building civil or infrastructure profile before presenting the model as domain-general.

The five accepted grok findings each rest on a narrower evidence base than the base findings around them (IFC property sets for life safety, a single ECHO dictionary for compliance status, one IBC section for occupancy authorization). Mark them as provisionally sourced in the draft and re-verify before they carry any normative weight.
deferredResearch: Whether one operational facility may span multiple sites, and by what method area, population and reporting are apportioned when a facility straddles parcels, municipalities, tribal land or utility service territories. Claude allows multi-site with apportionment but states no consulted source prescribes a method; grok records the question as unresolved. Neither position is evidenced, so it must be recorded as an open Dimension decision.

Accessibility designation at facility aggregate level (ISO 21542, ADA and national equivalents). Grok carries only the IFC HandicapAccessible flag and lists ISO 21542/ADA as an omission; claude does not address accessibility at all. Needs a primary source before any finding is created.

Ongoing statutory inspection regimes referenced but not sourced: NFPA 101, 25 and 72, ASME A17.1 and non-US equivalents. Required to give the accepted fire-life-safety finding a defensible inspection cadence rather than a static assertion.

Facility registers outside the US EPA FRS (European PRTR, national real-property inventories and cadastres) to test whether the identifier resolution, programme-interest and regulatory-standing structures survive substitution of the US instruments they were derived from.

Sustainability and green-building certification at facility rather than building level (LEED, BREEAM, EPBD energy performance certificates). Claude rejected it as attractive but insufficiently grounded; grok lists ENERGY STAR as unfetched. Decide only after a facility-level primary source is obtained.

Person-level occupancy, access credentials and workplace monitoring. Claude marks this an explicit coverage gap and holds only aggregate counts; verify whether even aggregate occupancy retention and publication are lawful in strict data-protection jurisdictions before the model is adopted there.

Insurance, valuation and loss-history context, and digital-twin runtime telemetry with control-point naming (Brick, Project Haystack). Both are acknowledged parts of the facility decision surface but neither provider found primary support for a defensible structure.
