bundles.name: Identity and Classification
bundles.description: What fixes which facility is meant, how it is named and designated, and how it is typed for operational, code and reporting purposes.
bundles.rationale: Facility data is federated across construction, real-property, regulatory and energy systems, each issuing its own key and its own typology. Identity resolution and classification precedence must be settled before any other context is trustworthy.

layers.name: Identity and Naming
layers.description: Authoritative keys, cross-registry references, human-readable names and structured reference designations for the facility.

findings.name: Facility identifier set and resolution rules
findings.description: The identifiers that pin a facility to a single real-world referent: the master-system key, governed registry identifiers issued by external authorities, and the rules for uniqueness, non-reuse, merge and split. EPA FRS demonstrates the pattern of assigning a registry identifier and then matching incoming program records to it.

findings.name: Facility naming and structured designation
findings.description: Human-readable names, aliases and signage names alongside structured reference designations formed under ISO 81346-12. Names are mutable and non-unique and must never be used as identity, while reference designations encode a position in a functional, product or location aspect structure.

layers.name: Classification and Typology
layers.description: Functional, industrial and regulatory typing of the facility, including building-code occupancy classification and its consequences.

findings.name: Functional and reporting classification
findings.description: The facility's primary function and any secondary uses, expressed in one or more governed schemes (IFC facility subtype, Uniclass Complexes/Entities, ENERGY STAR property type, industrial activity codes used for regulatory reporting), with an explicit precedence for each downstream purpose.

findings.name: Building-code occupancy and hazard classification
findings.description: The regulatory occupancy groups assigned under the applicable building code edition, construction type, mixed-occupancy treatment and the highest hazard class present. This classification is legally consequential and is asserted by an authority having jurisdiction, unlike operational typologies.

bundles.name: Spatial Extent and Composition
bundles.description: Where the facility is, what boundary defines it, what contains it and what it is made of.
bundles.rationale: Facility boundaries are the single most contested aspect of the model: they determine metering scope, regulatory scope, security perimeter and cost allocation. IFC, CityGML and INSPIRE each supply normative but differing spatial constructs that must be reconciled once, here.

layers.name: Geospatial Extent and Addressing
layers.description: Georeferenced geometry, coordinate reference and accuracy, together with addressing and the administrative jurisdictions the facility falls within.

findings.name: Facility geometry, georeference and level of detail
findings.description: The representative point and boundary geometry of the facility, the coordinate reference system and vertical datum, positional accuracy, and the level of detail at which geometry is held. CityGML supplies LoD semantics, INSPIRE supplies accuracy and elevation reference expectations, and IFC supplies relative placement against site or parent facility.

findings.name: Addressing and jurisdictional placement
findings.description: Addresses used for postal, service, regulatory and emergency purposes, plus the administrative and jurisdictional units the facility falls within, including cases where it straddles a boundary. Address values are references into a sibling Address model; only role, authority and jurisdiction assignment are held here.

layers.name: Composition, Systems and Asset Breakdown
layers.description: How the facility sits inside a site, decomposes into parts and buildings, and relates to its engineered systems and component asset register.

findings.name: Site containment and boundary exclusivity
findings.description: The typed edge from the containing Site to this Facility, whether that containment is exclusive, whether the facility spans multiple sites or parcels, and how facility identity survives site subdivision or amalgamation. IFC permits a facility with no site at all, so containment must be modelled as conditional.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Site containment is a typed edge between two independently governed models. The assertion carries only references, validity dates and an exclusivity flag; the documents of record (site plan, deed, survey) are artifacts of the Site model, and duplicating them here would create two conflicting masters for the same evidence.

findings.name: Facility part decomposition and building membership
findings.description: How the facility breaks down into parts and which buildings or structures are members over which periods. IFC requires an explicit usage convention for each facility part, and permits a facility to be part of a facility part, which allows longitudinal or regional division of larger facilities.

findings.name: Engineered systems and asset register linkage
findings.description: Facility-level engineered systems (power, HVAC, water, drainage, fire protection, security, communications), their structured reference designations, the spaces or parts they serve, and the linkage from facility to the component asset register that holds individual equipment items.

findings.name: Non-building, mobile and exclusion cases
findings.description: ISO 16739-1:2024 / IFC 4.3 extends facility to bridges, roads, railways, waterways and port facilities. FHIR includes mobile clinics, ambulances and vehicles. EPA includes monitoring stations and waste sites that cannot be classified as single facilities. ISO/TR 41013 states that a single asset such as a car or air-handling unit is not a facility, and that something not built, such as a nature preserve, is not a facility. Mobile versus fixed and instance versus kind must be explicit. Kind-of-location classifiers are out of scope as instances.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, State and Time
bundles.description: Where the facility is in its life, what condition it is in, and how record time is distinguished from real-world time.
bundles.rationale: Facility records are consumed long after they are written and are routinely corrected retroactively. Separating lifecycle phase, operational status, real-world validity and record versioning is required to make historic queries answerable and corrections auditable.

layers.name: Lifecycle Phase and Milestone Events
layers.description: Phase and status of the facility across its service life, and the milestone events that move it between them.

findings.name: Lifecycle phase, operational status and milestone events
findings.description: The facility's position in the ISO 15686-1 life cycle (initiation, project definition, design, construction, commissioning, operation, maintenance, refurbishment, replacement, deconstruction and disposal), its current operational status, and the milestone events that changed either. INSPIRE supplies a construction-condition code list and ISO 19650-3 supplies operational trigger events that require an information exchange.

layers.name: Condition, Service Life and Record Versioning
layers.description: Physical condition and remaining service life of the facility, and the versioning rules that govern its record over time.

findings.name: Condition assessment, service life and deferred maintenance
findings.description: Measured or estimated physical condition of the facility, the method and date of assessment, design and remaining service life, and the accumulated deferred maintenance liability. Federal real-property reporting requires condition and related measures alongside a reassessment cadence.

findings.name: Record versioning, valid time and observation time
findings.description: The bitemporal discipline for facility records: record version validity bounds, real-world validity, event time, observation time and ingestion time, and the rule separating a correction of a past error from a genuine real-world change. INSPIRE mandates lifespan version bounds with time-zone information; CityGML supplies a versioning module for city object states.

bundles.name: Authority, Tenure and Compliance
bundles.description: Who owns, holds and operates the facility, what it is authorised to do, and what may be disclosed about it.
bundles.rationale: A facility is simultaneously a property interest, an operating responsibility and a regulated object. These three chains of authority are frequently held by different organisations, and conflating them is the most common cause of unactionable facility data.

layers.name: Ownership, Custody and Operating Accountability
layers.description: Legal interest in the facility, custodial control, and the demand-organisation to service-provider accountability chain.

findings.name: Ownership, custody and legal interest
findings.description: The legal interest held in the facility (owned, leased, licensed or otherwise managed), the party holding title, the organisation with custody and control where different, and the encumbrances, easements and lease terms that constrain use. Federal real-property reporting treats legal interest, ownership and custodial agency as distinct reportable facts.

findings.name: Operator and facility-management accountability
findings.description: The chain from demand organisation to facility-management service provider, the scope of services delegated, the governing agreement, and the named accountable person for statutory duties. ISO 41011 makes the demand-organisation and service-provider distinction the core of facility-management vocabulary.

layers.name: Regulatory Standing and Compliance Evidence
layers.description: Regulatory programmes that apply to the facility, the authorisations it holds, and the inspection and certification evidence that demonstrates continuing compliance.

findings.name: Regulatory programme interests, permits and statutory inspections
findings.description: The regulatory programmes under which the facility is regulated or monitored, the programme identifiers issued by each regulator, the permits and authorisations in force with their validity and conditions, and the statutory inspection and certification regime with due dates, results and open nonconformities. EPA FRS models this as environmental interest types linking program records to a single facility registry identifier.

findings.name: Occupancy authorization and authority having jurisdiction
findings.description: Under IBC 111.1, a building or structure shall not be used or occupied, and a change of occupancy shall not be made, until the building official has issued a certificate of occupancy. Certificates that presume authority to violate the code are not valid. Work exempt from permit may be excepted. This rule is building-code-centric; roads, railways and some civil facilities are authorized by other AHJs. A CO authorizes occupancy under the building code; it does not by itself satisfy ongoing fire-code, elevator or environmental program duties. Phased projects may require occupancy authorization before occupying portions.

findings.name: Compliance monitoring status
findings.description: ECHO reports compliance monitoring activity counts, last monitoring date and statute-specific compliance status, including inactive facility. These determinations often reflect alleged rather than finally adjudicated violations. This finding is an alignment to US environmental operating data; it is not a universal compliance model and must not be treated as a court judgement.

layers.name: Security Posture and Information Access
layers.description: The facility's assessed security level and protective measures, and the constraints on disclosing facility information.

findings.name: Facility security level and protective posture
findings.description: The assessed security level of the facility derived from mission criticality, symbolism, facility population, facility size and threat to tenants, the baseline countermeasures that follow, implemented versus required status, and any accepted deviations. The ISC standard defines five levels with associated requirements.

findings.name: Information disclosure and access constraints
findings.description: Which facility attributes may be published, which must be withheld or generalised, on what legal basis, who may grant exceptions, and what must be logged. Federal real-property publication law expressly authorises excluding assets for national-security reasons and under freedom-of-information exemptions, establishing that facility inventories are not uniformly public.

bundles.name: Operations, Performance and Risk
bundles.description: How much the facility can do, how well it performs, how it is maintained and what threatens its continued operation.
bundles.rationale: Operating decisions and investment cases depend on capacity, utilisation, resource performance and criticality. Each of these is a measurement with a boundary, a method and an observation time, and is worthless without them.

layers.name: Capacity, Utilisation and Resource Performance
layers.description: Area and capacity measures, occupant population and operating schedule, and benchmarked resource and emissions performance with its measurement provenance.

findings.name: Area, capacity, occupancy and utilisation
findings.description: Area measures under a declared measurement standard, design capacity, occupant population by category, operating schedule and derived utilisation. Gross floor area and operating-hours style use details are the mandatory inputs to benchmarking, while facility population and size are two of the five security-level determination factors.

findings.name: Energy, water and emissions performance with measurement provenance
findings.description: Benchmarked resource and emissions performance for the facility over stated reporting periods, the normalisation and benchmark reference used, the metering boundary relative to the facility boundary, and the share of values that are metered rather than estimated. Multi-building facilities are benchmarked as a parent property aggregating child buildings, which makes the boundary declaration mandatory rather than optional.

findings.name: Performance evaluation and service life
findings.description: Service life is the period after installation during which a building or its parts meet performance requirements. Post-occupancy evaluation analyses how functional and comfortable a building is after users have occupied it. ISO 19650-3 includes post-occupancy or implementation evaluation as a point on the operational timeline. Key performance indicators and indoor environmental quality are measurement alignments; detailed energy-benchmarking schemes such as ENERGY STAR are known omissions unless later aligned.

layers.name: Maintenance, Risk and Continuity
layers.description: How the facility is maintained, how critical it is, what hazards it faces and how operation continues when it is impaired.

findings.name: Maintenance strategy and work management linkage
findings.description: The maintenance strategy applied per system, the planned maintenance tasks and their frequencies, the linkage from work orders back to facility, system and component, and the maintenance backlog with its ageing profile. Handover data schemas carry planned job, resource and event tables that seed this regime at commissioning.

findings.name: Criticality, hazard exposure and operational continuity
findings.description: The facility's criticality or mission-dependency rating and the method behind it, the natural and human-caused hazards it is exposed to, redundancy and alternate-facility arrangements, and when continuity plans were last exercised. Criticality drives both asset-management investment prioritisation and the mission-criticality factor in security-level determination.

findings.name: Fire, life safety and risk
findings.description: IfcFacility may carry Pset_SpaceFireSafetyRequirements (fire risk factor, flammable storage, fire exit, sprinkler protection, air pressurization) and Pset_Risk (likelihood, consequence, mitigation). These are facility-scale assertions and do not replace storey- or space-level life-safety design. ISO 41011 emergency preparedness is the capability to mitigate emergency consequences. National fire-code inspection programs such as NFPA 25 or 72 are known omissions as primary sources.

bundles.name: Information Governance and Interoperability
bundles.description: What information about the facility must exist, where it came from, how long it is kept, and how it moves between standards and systems.
bundles.rationale: Facility data outlives the systems that hold it and is exchanged across construction, operations, regulatory and geospatial domains. Requirements, provenance, retention and alignment must be governed explicitly or the model degrades into an unverifiable snapshot.

layers.name: Information Requirements, Provenance and Quality
layers.description: What information is required about the facility, where each value came from, and whether it can be trusted.

findings.name: Asset information requirements and accepted deliverables
findings.description: The organisational, asset and exchange information requirements that apply to this facility, the trigger events during operation that require an information exchange, the asset information model held for the facility, and how information is accepted or rejected. ISO 19650-3 establishes asset information requirements at asset level and exchange information requirements per appointment and trigger event.

findings.name: Attribute provenance, source precedence and validation
findings.description: Per-attribute lineage to the supplying source system, the precedence rule when sources disagree, the validation rules a facility record must pass before publication, and the confidence attached to matched or derived values. Federated registries demonstrate the need: values are integrated from many program systems, matched, and periodically re-selected by an automated best-pick process.

layers.name: Standards Alignment, Retention and Exchange
layers.description: How facility context maps to external standards, how long each record class is kept, and how the model is projected into any storage or interface technology.

findings.name: External standard alignments and crosswalk fidelity
findings.description: The external schemas, ontologies and classifications this model is aligned to, at which versions, whether each mapping is lossless, which concepts have no faithful counterpart, and what evidence would be required before asserting conformance. Notably, the widely used building topology vocabulary has no facility class between site and building, and IFC subordinates buildings to facilities by type rather than by aggregation.

findings.name: Retention, disposition and archival transfer
findings.description: Which retention schedule governs each class of facility record, the disposition trigger and period, which records are permanent rather than temporary, and how destruction is evidenced. Government-wide scheduling treats routine facility operation and maintenance records as temporary with destruction three years after creation or supersession, while requiring the oldest records be offered for archival transfer before any disposition is applied.

findings.name: Canonical payload, packaging and interface neutrality
findings.description: The canonical logical payload of a facility record independent of any serialisation, how artifacts are packaged and integrity-checked, how partial updates are expressed and validated, and the bootstrap manifest that must accompany any store. Handover schemas that publish equivalent content as spreadsheet, model-file and JSON demonstrate that meaning must be defined before format.

model.name: Site / Campus
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to identify, describe, govern and operate a site or campus: a bounded area of land (with associated subsurface, surface water and airspace) held under coordinated management control, inside which facilities, infrastructure, circulation and open space are operated as one unit.
model.scope_statement: WM-BLT-008 models the managed physical container itself - its identity, classification, spatial extent, composition, control, lifecycle, operating conditions, measurement boundary and evidence - and stops at the interfaces with contained facilities (WM-BLT-006), the containing settlement or place (WM-PLC-005 / WM-PLC-002), the legal land unit, and the parties that own or operate it. Facilities, parcels, organisations, permits and individual assets are referenced by identifier, never re-modelled here. The model is projection-independent: IFC, CityGML, GeoJSON, Markdown, Git, MCP and MongoDB are encodings of these semantics, not the semantics.
in_scope: Site identity, naming, coding and identifier crosswalks across authoritative registries and internal systems
Site typology and classification against governed schemes
Declared managed extent: what is inside the site, including discontiguous parts and third-party enclaves
Boundary geometry, coordinate reference system, elevation datum, vertical and subsurface extent
References to the land parcels and tenure instruments the site rests on
Containment of facilities (WM-BLT-006) and on-site infrastructure networks
Ground surface, landscape, open space, parking and laydown areas
Internal zones, precincts, development phases, circulation routes and control points
Ownership, operatorship, duty-holder accountability and delegation
Regulatory authorisations, permits and registry interests attached to the site
Physical access control, perimeter and site information sensitivity
Lifecycle states, boundary change events, split/merge and successor lineage
Operating hours, site rules, permit-to-work regimes and service provision
Natural hazard exposure, contamination and environmental constraints
Emergency preparedness, evacuation and muster arrangements
Site-level quantities, areas, occupancy and capacity
Energy, water, waste and greenhouse-gas reporting boundary and meter coverage
Site-scale monitoring platforms and observations
Site records, evidence, provenance and retention
Alignment and crosswalks to external schemas and operational systems
out_of_scope: Internal anatomy of a building or civil facility - storeys, spaces, rooms, systems and building elements (WM-BLT-006 and its children)
Legal land title, deeds, rights, restrictions and responsibilities as first-class legal objects (land administration sibling model, aligned to ISO 19152-1)
Settlement, administrative area and populated-place semantics (WM-PLC-005, WM-PLC-002)
Legal entity, organisation and person records for owners, operators, staff, visitors and contractors
Individual equipment and plant items, their maintenance history and work orders (asset register and maintenance sibling models)
Construction and capital project delivery processes, programmes and contracts
Lease, licence and other commercial agreement terms
Address and geocoding conceptual model - addresses are referenced, not defined here
Utility network topology, capacity modelling and operations beyond the site demarcation point
Sensor and actuator device specifications - observations are referenced through SOSA/SSN patterns
Environmental permit legal instruments as documents of record (authorisation sibling model)
Financial valuation, depreciation and real-estate investment accounting

boundary_notes.distinction: IFC 4.3 keeps IfcSite and IfcFacility as separate spatial structure elements: a facility is aggregated by IfcProject, IfcSite or another IfcFacility, and decomposes into IfcFacilityPart and IfcSpace. WM-BLT-008 therefore records the containment edge, the facility identifier and the site-side demarcation point, and never re-states facility-internal structure.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Land parcel / cadastral parcel (land administration sibling model)
boundary_notes.distinction: A cadastral parcel is a legal spatial unit with homogeneous property rights, identified by nationalCadastralReference and inspireId, and used primarily as a locator. A site is a management construct: it may span many parcels, occupy part of a parcel, or include parcels held under different tenure. IFC 4.3 deprecated IfcSite.LandTitleNumber, reinforcing that title belongs elsewhere. WM-BLT-008 references parcels; it does not model rights, restrictions or responsibilities.

A settlement is an administrative or populated-place concept; a site is an operational container under a single management regime. A site can straddle two settlements or lie wholly outside any populated place, so containment by settlement is a recorded relationship with its own evidence, not a derived truth.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Regulatory facility registry entries (e.g. EPA FRS facility site)
boundary_notes.distinction: EPA FRS clusters program-system records under a 12-digit Registry ID and treats the originating programs as source of truth. A regulatory facility site is a reporting unit that frequently does not align one-to-one with the managed site: one site may carry several FRS interests, and one FRS record may cover only part of a site. The crosswalk must be recorded with match confidence rather than assumed.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Reporting boundary constructs (ENERGY STAR property, GHG Protocol organizational boundary)
boundary_notes.distinction: EPA Portfolio Manager models a campus as a parent property with child properties and does not support nested campuses; GHG Protocol sets organizational boundaries by equity share or control. Both are accounting boundaries that can diverge from the physical managed extent. WM-BLT-008 records each reporting boundary as a distinct, dated view over the site, never as the site's definition.

On-site distribution is in scope only up to the demarcation point where responsibility passes to an external network operator. Network topology, hydraulic or electrical modelling and upstream operations sit in the utility network sibling model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Asset management system (ISO 55001) and asset information model (ISO 19650)
boundary_notes.distinction: ISO 55001 governs the management system and ISO 19650 governs information containers and trigger events. WM-BLT-008 is neither: it is the subject those systems act upon. It records which management system and information requirements apply, and cites their identifiers, without absorbing their clauses.

functions.name: Register a site
functions.description: Create a governed site record and assign its canonical identifier under the identity priority rule.
inputs: Candidate authoritative identifiers from master systems
preconditions: A search for existing site records has been run and no duplicate confirmed
At least one owning or operating party reference resolves
The managed extent statement has an authoring role
effects: Site identifier reserved and marked active
Registration event appended to the site change log
Site becomes eligible for containment, authorisation and reporting links

functions.name: Define or revise the site boundary
functions.description: Record boundary geometry with a declared coordinate reference system, vertical datum, positional accuracy and survey provenance.
outputs: Site reference point and reference elevation
preconditions: Site record exists and is not in a closed state
Coordinate reference system and vertical datum are both declared
Survey provenance identifies the surveying organisation and date
effects: Previous boundary version superseded and retained
Derived areas flagged for recalculation
Downstream zone and route geometries flagged for revalidation

functions.name: Attach or detach a facility
functions.description: Create or end a containment edge between the site and a facility record in WM-BLT-006, with relationship type and effective period.
preconditions: Facility identifier resolves in the facility model
Facility geometry lies within or is justified against the managed extent
No conflicting exclusive containment exists elsewhere
effects: Facility appears in site composition views
Reporting boundary recalculation triggered
Change appended to the site change log with event and record times

functions.name: Transition site lifecycle state
functions.description: Move the site to a new state in the controlled vocabulary with authorisation, evidence and separately recorded effective and record times.
preconditions: Target state is reachable from the current state
Required evidence artifacts exist and are current
Authorising role holds the delegated authority
effects: Prior state retained as history
Downstream obligations such as monitoring and reporting re-evaluated
Notifications raised to regulatory registry holders where required

functions.name: Split, merge or transfer part of a site
functions.description: Reorganise site records while preserving predecessor and successor lineage and reassigning contained facilities, authorisations and reporting boundaries.
outputs: Reassignment schedule for facilities and authorisations
preconditions: Boundary geometry for every resulting site is defined
Every contained facility and authorisation has a declared destination
Change is authorised under the extent authority rule
effects: Superseded site identifiers retired but never reassigned
Reporting boundaries restated with an explicit restatement note
Crosswalks to external registries flagged for reconciliation

functions.name: Reconcile external site identifiers
functions.description: Match the site against candidate records in external registries and operational systems and record match confidence and unresolved conflicts.
preconditions: Site has a primary identifier and boundary geometry or reference point
Target system snapshot has a stated extraction timestamp
effects: Crosswalk table updated with reconciliation timestamp
Below-threshold matches queued for manual review
Extent misalignments recorded against registry interests

functions.name: Grant or revoke physical site access
functions.description: Issue, amend or revoke a physical access authorisation scoped to the site or a security zone, and enforce it at designated entry and exit points.
preconditions: Requested zones exist in the current zoning plan
Induction and competence evidence is valid at the effective date
Authorising role is designated for the requested zones
effects: Enforcement updated at designated entry and exit points
Access events logged against the authorisation
Revocation triggers device inventory and combination change checks

functions.name: Record a site observation
functions.description: Ingest an observation against a site feature of interest with its phenomenon time and result time held separately.
outputs: Observation record appended to the relevant series
preconditions: Sensor is registered in the monitoring plan
Both phenomenon time and result time are supplied in RFC 3339 with offset or Z
Calibration record for the sensor is current
effects: Series statistics and gap tracking updated
Threshold breaches raised as events
Regulatory monitoring obligations progressed

functions.name: Compile a reporting boundary and return
functions.description: Assemble a scheme-specific reporting boundary from parent and child properties, meter coverage and allocation rules, and produce the reportable dataset.
preconditions: Every facility in the boundary has a declared inclusion decision
Campus-serving meters are recorded at the parent level
Consolidation approach is declared and unchanged within the period or the change is disclosed
effects: Reportable dataset versioned and locked for the period
Restatements recorded against prior periods where methods changed
Divergence from managed extent explicitly stated

functions.name: Validate a site record
functions.description: Run structural, referential and temporal validation over the site record and report defects against declared rules.
preconditions: Validation rule set version is declared
Referenced sibling models are reachable or their unavailability is recorded
effects: Defects raised for remediation with owners
Records failing mandatory rules blocked from publication
Validation history retained as evidence

functions.name: Close a site and apply retention
functions.description: Move a site to a closed state and apply the retention and disposal schedule to its records, retaining what regulation requires.
outputs: Closed site record with closure timestamp
preconditions: No active authorisation requires an operating site
Contamination and remediation position is recorded
Successor responsibility for retained obligations is assigned
effects: Site identifier retired and never reassigned
Records outside retention disposed under authorisation
Retained records marked with their retention expiry

functions.name: Assign party roles
functions.description: Record owner, operator, occupier and LADM RRR, and optionally transfer AIM on ownership change.
preconditions: Parties are identified in a party register
Instruments exist for ownership claims
effects: Ownership and operatorship are current
ISO 19650-3 continuity obligation is either fulfilled or recorded as a gap

functions.name: Bind cadastral units
functions.description: Associate LandID, LandTitleID, INSPIRE locators or LADM spatial units and optional SpatialUnitGroup without collapsing legal parcels.
preconditions: Statutory identifiers are well-formed for the jurisdiction
Informal units are explicitly flagged
effects: Legal substrate is referenced
Operational geometry remains independent

functions.name: Compose site structure
functions.description: Set COMPLEX/ELEMENT/PARTIAL composition and parent/child site relations, including disconnected members of a campus complex.
preconditions: Referenced sites exist
Composition types respect IFC COMPLEX/ELEMENT/PARTIAL stacking
effects: Aggregation edges are written
Campus aggregation mode is recorded

functions.name: Record environmental status
functions.description: Attach a contamination or statutory-facility overlay, affected geometry and responsible parties.
preconditions: Overlay is not used to replace site or facility class
effects: CERCLA/RCRA or equivalent overlay is queryable
Occupancy and transfer constraints are visible

composition.purpose: Site / Campus specialises the generic place concept, inheriting spatial referencing and naming semantics while adding managed-container behaviour.
Records the settlement or populated place that spatially contains the site, as an evidenced relationship rather than a derived truth, since a site may straddle or fall outside settlement boundaries.
The site aggregates facility records; IFC 4.3 confirms a facility may be aggregated by a site and that facility-internal structure belongs to the facility.

composition.target: Land administration / property right sibling model (LADM-aligned)
composition.purpose: Supplies parcels, basic administrative units, parties and rights, responsibilities and restrictions that the site references but must not re-model.
Resolves owner, operator, duty holder, service provider and regulator references; site identity must never be conflated with the operating legal entity.
Supplies typed addresses for postal, delivery, emergency and registered purposes; IFC deprecated the site-embedded address attribute, reinforcing external ownership of addressing.

composition.target: Authorisation, permit and licence sibling model
composition.purpose: Holds permits, licences and consents as legal instruments; the site records only which authorisations apply, their validity and their operational conditions.

composition.target: Asset register and maintenance sibling model
composition.purpose: Holds individual plant and equipment items and their work history; the site provides the location and management context under ISO 55001 rather than the asset records themselves.
Owns external network topology and operations; the site records only on-site distribution and the demarcation point where responsibility transfers.
Supplies Platform, Sensor, Observation, FeatureOfInterest and the normative separation of phenomenon time from result time, reused rather than redefined by this model.
Supplies the versioned-object pattern with beginLifespanVersion and endLifespanVersion alongside real-world validFrom and validTo, keeping event time and record time distinct.
Alignment target for spatial structure, composition type and site reference geometry. Alignment only: LandTitleNumber and SiteAddress are deprecated in IFC 4.3 and are not carried forward.
Alignment target for encoding-independent geospatial representation, city object grouping, land use and relief at site scale.
Alignment target for parcel referencing and lifespan versioning attributes when operating in the European regulatory context.
Alignment target for management-system scope, accountability, life-cycle planning and control of change applied to the site as a managed object.
Alignment target for information containers, suitability status, the common data environment as agreed source of information, and the trigger-event update pattern.

composition.target: GHG Protocol Corporate Standard boundary rules
composition.purpose: Alignment target for organizational and operational boundary setting when a site emissions inventory is compiled.

Alignment target for regulatory site identification and crosswalk reconciliation in the United States context; the FRS Registry ID is a master-system identifier candidate, not a global site identifier.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name a single accountable owner for the site model package and a named deputy, consistent with ISO 55001 assignment of responsibility and authority.
The package must declare its scope boundary against WM-BLT-006, WM-PLC-005 and the land administration sibling model, and must not redefine elements owned by those models.
The package must publish its identifier policy, stating the master systems it recognises, its governed global identifier schemes and its fallback UUID or ULID generator.
The package must declare a validation rule set version and the common data environment that acts as the agreed source of information for site records.
The package must maintain a register of alignments and conformance claims, distinguishing evidenced conformance from declared alignment.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one stable namespace per adopting Dimension, with a path segment for the model (site) and never a path segment for storage format or interface. Identifiers minted by the Dimension are opaque and are never derived from names, addresses, coordinates or dates. External identifiers are carried in a namespaced crosswalk, never merged into the local identifier space. Namespace changes require a redirect and a recorded supersession, since retired site identifiers are never reassigned.
registry_links: vr.wm-blt-008 (this model) in the world-model record plane
WM-BLT-006 Facility as the contained-model registry entry
WM-PLC-002 Place and WM-PLC-005 Settlement as parent and containing registry entries
External registry references recorded per instance: national cadastral register, EPA Facility Registry Service, and any benchmarking scheme property registry

canonicalization_rules: Canonical form is the format-neutral logical record; JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, IFC, CityGML, Git objects and MongoDB documents are projections and never authoritative.
All timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; local wall-clock times without offset are rejected at ingest.
Geometry is canonicalised to a single declared coordinate reference system per record, with the CRS identifier stored alongside; reprojected copies are derived artifacts.
Collections are ordered deterministically by identifier for hashing; ordering carries no semantics unless a rank attribute is present.
Absent values are represented as absent, never as empty strings, zero or a sentinel date; a value that is deliberately withheld is marked withheld with a reason.
patch_rules: Every change is expressed as an addressed patch against a specific record version, carrying both the event time and the record time.
Identifier fields are immutable; a correction to a primary identifier is a supersession event with predecessor and successor links, not an in-place edit.
Boundary geometry, lifecycle state and accountability changes require an authorising role reference on the patch and are rejected without one.
Patches to reported quantities within a closed reporting period are recorded as restatements with an explicit reason, not as silent overwrites.
Patches are append-only in the change log; the log is never rewritten, and rollbacks are expressed as compensating patches.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional element or a new coded value is a minor change; removing an element, tightening cardinality or narrowing a code list is a breaking change.
Deprecated elements are retained and marked with their deprecating version and replacement, following the IFC precedent for LandTitleNumber and SiteAddress.
Consumers must ignore unknown elements rather than fail, and must not infer meaning from element ordering.
A crosswalk is versioned against both the source model version and the target schema version; a target schema upgrade invalidates the crosswalk until re-verified.
No conformance to an external standard is claimed without a cited test or certification artifact; otherwise the relationship is recorded as alignment only.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the site, for example an EPA FRS Registry ID or a national cadastral reference held by the responsible authority.
Governed global identifier or IRI from a maintained scheme, for example an INSPIRE external object identifier or an IFC GlobalId, where a persistence and non-reallocation policy exists.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only where no higher-priority identifier exists and recorded with the justification for its use.
A date, a name, an address, a coordinate pair or a file path is never an identifier and must not be used as a key.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded in RFC 3339 format with seconds precision and an explicit UTC offset or Z. Event time (when the thing happened in the world) and observation or ingestion time (when the system learned of it) are recorded as separate fields wherever they can differ, following the SOSA separation of phenomenon time from result time. Date-only values are used solely where the source itself is date-only and are labelled as such.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named as <site-identifier>/<artifact-class>/<sequence-or-period>/<revision>, where sequence is monotonically increasing within the site and revision is issued by the producing party. Reporting artifacts substitute the RFC 3339 period start and end for sequence. Sequence numbers are never reused after retirement, and gaps are permitted and explained rather than backfilled.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest over its canonical form, the producing party, the approving role and the approval timestamp. Superseded revisions are retained with a link to their successor and are never deleted before the retention period expires. Redacted derivatives carry a reference to their parent digest and the identifier of the redaction profile applied, so that any published extract can be traced to a controlled original.

policies: Boundaries and containment are recorded as authored, evidenced decisions with an authorising role, never inferred from geometry alone; a facility whose footprint falls inside the boundary is not thereby part of the site.
Legal, regulatory and commercial constructs are referenced by identifier and never re-modelled inside the site record; the site model holds applicability, validity and operational consequence only.

No conformance to an external standard is asserted without cited evidence; unevidenced relationships are recorded as alignments and any conflict between standards is recorded rather than resolved silently.
Security-sensitive site information is classified before publication, and any externally shared derivative is produced through an approved redaction profile traceable to its controlled original.
Reporting boundaries are maintained as dated views over the site and are never allowed to overwrite or redefine the managed extent.
Physical site records default to operator-controlled access; cadastral extracts follow the originating jurisdiction's disclosure law.
Security-minded redaction of gates, utilities and occupancy applies to sensitive campuses before any public city-model publication.
Temporary construction and contamination overlays expire or close by explicit state change; they are never deleted silently while legal obligations remain.
Ownership transfer must attempt AIM continuity per ISO 19650-3; failure is recorded as a governed gap, not ignored.

read: Read of non-sensitive site identity, classification, boundary and composition is available to any authenticated agent within the adopting Dimension.
Read of security-sensitive elements including perimeter detail, access authorisations, access logs and buried-service records requires an explicit named grant and is logged.
Read of a superseded revision requires the same or stronger grant as the current revision and returns the supersession link.
Bulk read and export require a declared purpose, and any export crossing a Dimension boundary is produced through an approved redaction profile.
create: Site records are created only through the register-site function, which enforces the identity priority rule and a duplicate check.
Containment edges to facilities are created only where the facility identifier resolves and no conflicting exclusive containment exists.
Observations are created only for sensors registered in the current monitoring plan and only with both phenomenon time and result time supplied.
Artifacts are created with a content digest, producing party and approval record; artifacts without provenance are rejected.
update: Identifier fields are immutable; changes are expressed as supersession with predecessor and successor links.
Boundary, lifecycle state, accountability and extent changes require an authorising role and supporting evidence artifacts.
Updates carry both event time and record time; an update supplying only one of the two is rejected where they can differ.
Updates within a closed reporting period are recorded as restatements with a stated reason and do not overwrite the locked period dataset.
delete: Logical deletion only: records are retired or superseded, never physically removed while within their retention period.
Physical disposal occurs only under the approved retention and disposal schedule, with a recorded disposal authorisation, action and timestamp.
Retired site identifiers are permanently reserved and are never reassigned to a different site.
Deletion is blocked while any active authorisation, unresolved regulatory obligation or open legal hold references the record.

roles.name: Site model owner
responsibilities: Owns the model package, its scope boundary and its versioning
Approves breaking changes and deprecations
Maintains the register of alignments and conformance claims

roles.name: Site data steward
responsibilities: Maintains identifier assignment, crosswalks and reconciliation against external registries
Adjudicates below-threshold matches and records unresolved conflicts
Monitors completeness and currency of site records

roles.name: Site operator or facility manager
responsibilities: Maintains managed extent, containment, zoning, operating model and service arrangements
Authorises physical access within delegated limits
Ensures emergency and permit-to-work arrangements are current

roles.name: Geospatial and survey authority
responsibilities: Approves boundary geometry, coordinate reference system and vertical datum declarations
Certifies positional accuracy and survey provenance
Validates divergence between the operational boundary and legal parcel lines

roles.name: Compliance and reporting officer
responsibilities: Maintains the authorisation register and regulatory registry interests
Defines and locks reporting boundaries and consolidation approaches
Owns restatements, assurance evidence and submission records

roles.name: Security and information classification authority
responsibilities: Classifies site information by sensitivity and approves redaction profiles
Governs access grants to security-sensitive elements and audits their use
Adjudicates conflicts between disclosure obligations and security restrictions

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Access is granted per scope to a named role for a stated purpose and a bounded period; grants at bundle scope do not cascade automatically to security-classified findings or artifacts within them.
exceptions: Emergency response override: designated emergency roles and external responders receive immediate read of emergency, hazard, muster and circulation findings during a declared incident, with the override logged and reviewed afterwards.

Mandatory disclosure: information subject to a statutory publication or access-on-request obligation is released through the approved channel even where the operator would prefer to withhold it, with any permitted exemption recorded.
Regulator access: an authority holding a registry interest in the site receives read of the findings within its remit without a per-request grant, scoped to that remit.

Security withholding: perimeter detail, access authorisations, access logs, buried-service records and security-zone geometry are withheld from general and bulk read even where the containing bundle is otherwise readable.
Legal hold: records under legal hold are readable to the holding authority and are exempt from scheduled disposal until the hold is lifted.
Emergency responders may read access-regime, gate and affected-geometry under recorded emergency-access exceptions.
Statutory cadastral publication may disclose parcel geometry even when campus security policy would redact operational fences.
Temporary construction wage-law envelopes may be disclosed to labour authorities without granting full AIM access.
audit_requirements: Every read of a security-classified finding or artifact is logged with actor, scope, purpose, RFC 3339 timestamp and grant reference.
Every write is logged with actor, authorising role, event time, record time and the change log sequence number it produced.
Every export crossing a Dimension boundary is logged with the redaction profile applied and the digest of both the parent and the derivative.
Emergency overrides and mandatory-disclosure releases are reviewed within a defined period after the event and the review outcome is recorded.
Audit logs are append-only, retained under the retention and disposal schedule, and are themselves subject to access control.
Log create, update, delete, overlay and mapping changes with actor, event time and ingestion time.
Log reads of security-sensitive geometry and environmental listings.
Retain audit logs at least as long as the AIM archive obligation for the site.

required_fields: Access default rule and classification scheme
read_order: AGENTS.md - establishes name, type and the four resolving URLs before any other action
Specification URL - the format-neutral model semantics, scope, exclusions and boundary notes
Storage type URL - how the current projection encodes the model, whether JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MongoDB or an IFC or CityGML exchange
Interface URL - the available read and write operations, authentication and the access default rule
Processes URL - the governed functions, their preconditions, authorising roles and effects
Alignment and crosswalk register - target schema versions, mapping losses and any conflicts before attempting exchange
Validation rule set - the rules a record must satisfy before publication

coverage.claim: Covers identity, classification, managed extent, spatial basis and georeferencing, land basis with planning controls, composition, control and access, lifecycle including temporary construction overlays, hazards and emergency response, measurement and reporting boundary, evidence and interoperability for a managed site or campus. Bounded to the container: legal land units, facility internals, parties, permits-as-instruments and individual assets are referenced by identifier, never re-modelled. No claim of universal completeness across jurisdictions or site types; marine, subsurface and relocatable sites remain an open gap, and alignment to cited standards is declared, not conformance-evidenced.

checklist.notes: Identity priority, master-system identifiers, governed global identifiers, UUID/ULID fallback, naming, retirement and non-reassignment are covered by the site-identity-and-designation finding and artifact_rules.identity_priority, grounded in EPA FRS (SRC-003), INSPIRE inspireId (SRC-004) and IFC GlobalId semantics (SRC-001).

State vocabulary, transition authority and evidence, split/merge lineage and trigger events are covered, grounded in ISO 55001 control of change (SRC-009) and ISO 19650 trigger events (SRC-012). The specific state vocabulary itself is an adopter decision and is marked as such rather than asserted.

Containment to facilities, reference to settlement and place, parcel coverage, adjacency, connection points and third-party enclaves are covered, grounded in IFC aggregation rules (SRC-001, SRC-002) and INSPIRE parcel locator semantics (SRC-004).

RFC 3339 with explicit offset or Z is mandated; event time and record time are held separately, reinforced by the SOSA phenomenonTime/resultTime distinction (SRC-005) and INSPIRE validFrom/beginLifespanVersion pairing (SRC-004).

Producing party, inputs, method, approval and content digest are required for artifacts; survey provenance and register verification dates are explicit. Grounded in ISO 19650 information containers (SRC-012) and EPA FRS source-system precedence (SRC-003).

Owner, operator, duty holder and delegation are separated with effective dates, grounded in ISO 55001 (SRC-009) and the LADM party and basic-administrative-unit separation (SRC-010). Legal title itself is explicitly out of scope.

A validate-site-record function, declared rule set versioning, match thresholds, conformance-evidence questions and publication blocking on mandatory-rule failure are all present (SRC-012, SRC-004, SRC-003).
Deny-by-default with four scopes, five exception classes and five audit requirements, grounded in the NIST SP 800-53 PE control pattern (SRC-007) and the ISO 19650 common data environment (SRC-012).

Retention periods with triggers and legal basis, disposal authorisation, logical-only deletion, permanent identifier reservation and legal hold are covered (SRC-007, SRC-003, SRC-009). Specific statutory retention durations are jurisdiction-dependent and are deliberately not asserted.

Alignment declarations, mapping-loss notes, matching rules, deprecated-element handling and an explicit alignment-not-conformance policy are covered against IFC (SRC-001, SRC-002), CityGML (SRC-008), INSPIRE (SRC-004), FRS (SRC-003), ISO 19650 (SRC-012) and GHG Protocol (SRC-013).

Scheme-versioned classification, multi-classification precedence, IFC composition type and reclassification triggers are covered (SRC-001, SRC-008, SRC-014). No single universal site typology is asserted, because none was found in the primary sources.

Boundary geometry, CRS, vertical datum, positional accuracy, reference point and vertical or subsurface extent are covered (SRC-001, SRC-004, SRC-008). Three-dimensional site volumes are supported conceptually but their encoding is left to the projection.
Areas, occupancy, capacity, meter coverage, allocation and consolidation approach are covered with mandatory measurement basis and date (SRC-011, SRC-013, SRC-004).

Perimeter, access authorisation, logging, device inventory and information sensitivity are covered from NIST SP 800-53 PE controls (SRC-007), including the disclosure-versus-security conflict resolution path.

Written plan requirement, evacuation and exit route assignment, employee accounting, alarm system and review triggers are taken directly from 29 CFR 1910.38 (SRC-006). This is US-specific and is flagged under regional assumptions.

Valuation, rent, service charge and capital planning belong to real-estate and finance sibling models. No primary source reviewed places commercial terms within a managed-site container model, so no structure is proposed here.

IFC 4.3 introduces IfcMarineFacility (SRC-002) and CityGML has WaterBody (SRC-008), but no primary source reviewed defines a managed-site container for offshore platforms, underground mines or relocatable sites. The vertical-extent and water-body elements are provided as a partial accommodation and this remains an unresolved boundary.

known_omissions: No governed global location identifier scheme is prescribed. GS1 GLN was investigated as a candidate but gs1.org returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt, so no GLN allocation rule is cited or relied upon anywhere in this model.

Reference designation systems for construction works (the ISO/IEC 81346 series, including RDS-CW) would give a rigorous site-to-facility-to-system designation grammar, but the texts are paywalled and no free normative extract was obtainable, so no designation grammar is asserted.

Buried-service record quality is modelled as a coded confidence level without binding it to a specific quality-level standard, because no freely readable normative source for subsurface utility record quality levels was verified in this session.
Waste, water discharge and air emission permit content is referenced but not decomposed; the decomposition belongs to an authorisation sibling model that does not yet exist in the registry.
Site-level accessibility requirements are limited to a question about designated accessible routes. No accessibility standard was cited as primary, so no requirement structure is proposed.
Biodiversity net gain, ecological baseline and habitat accounting appear only as protected-feature constraints; they may warrant their own layer in jurisdictions where they are mandatory.
The ENERGY STAR campus rules were read from the EPA landing page and EPA-published summaries; the guide PDF itself was not machine-readable in this session, so clause-level wording is not quoted.
No primary international feature type named Campus; higher-education, hospital and data-centre campus information models were not adopted as canonical classes.
Military installation and NATO/DoD site schemas were not retrieved as primary sources.
OSHA establishment combining nearby locations was only partially retrieved because eCFR blocked a full fetch; workplace mapping is therefore thinner than access policy.
Customary and informal tenure is acknowledged via LADM but not operationalised with a regional code list.
3D/4D cadastral air rights and subsurface volumes lack a single implementable geometry profile in this model.
Wet-infrastructure networks are out of LandInfra's initial release and remain out of this site model except as easements.
Biodiversity, occupancy, valuation (LADM Part 4) and climate normals are sibling models.
Seveso/IED, UK COMAH and other non-US contamination regimes are not cited as primary overlays.
IFC Pset_SiteWeather exists but weather is treated as observation, not as a climate sibling, and was not expanded.
conflicts: IFC 4.3 deprecates IfcSite.LandTitleNumber and IfcSite.SiteAddress (SRC-001), while many operational systems and earlier IFC exchanges still populate them. This model treats title and address as external references and records the deprecation as an explicit import and export handling rule rather than carrying the attributes forward.

EPA Portfolio Manager supports only a two-level parent and child property structure with no nested campuses (SRC-011), whereas IFC permits recursive site decomposition through COMPLEX, ELEMENT and PARTIAL composition types (SRC-001). The model keeps physical composition recursive and treats the benchmarking structure as a separate, flatter reporting view.

A regulatory facility site in EPA FRS is a reporting unit clustered from roughly ninety program systems (SRC-003) and frequently does not align one-to-one with a managed site. The model records extent alignment and match confidence rather than assuming identity between the two.

GHG Protocol organizational boundaries set by equity share or control (SRC-013) can include facilities the site operator does not manage and exclude ones it does. The model therefore forbids a reporting boundary from redefining the managed extent.

LADM treats the spatial unit as the carrier of rights and defines land administration around basic administrative units (SRC-010), whereas a managed site is defined by operational control. Where the two diverge the model records both, and does not attempt to reconcile them into a single boundary.

OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38 (SRC-006) permits an oral emergency action plan for employers with ten or fewer employees, which conflicts with the general expectation elsewhere in this model that controlling arrangements exist as retained artifacts. The finding records the requirement basis explicitly rather than mandating a written artifact universally.
IEC 62264/ISA-95 Site may be logical; ISO 6707-1 and IfcSite are physical land or water.
CERCLA 'facility' includes 'any site or area'; ISO 41011 'facility' is a collection of assets; Vercy WM-BLT-006 is the latter.
INSPIRE cadastral parcel (homogeneous unique ownership) often does not coincide with a multi-parcel or multi-owner campus.
IfcSite.RefLatitude/RefLongitude/RefElevation are approximate WGS84; IfcMapConversion is authoritative and may disagree.
IFC4.3 ADD2 deprecates LandTitleNumber and SiteAddress that remain in widespread IFC2x3/IFC4 data.
29 CFR 5.2 site of the work can include off-campus secondary fabrication sites that are not part of the permanent holding.
CityGML LandUse is land cover/use, not a managed operator holding; grouping via CityObjectGroup is not equivalent to IfcSite.
regional_assumptions: The emergency preparedness finding is grounded in United States federal OSHA regulation (SRC-006). Other jurisdictions impose different minimum content, review cycles and written-plan thresholds; the finding structure is intended to be jurisdiction-neutral but its specific elements are US-derived.

Regulatory site identification is grounded in the US EPA Facility Registry Service (SRC-003). Equivalent national registries exist elsewhere with different identifier structures, matching rules and authority models.

Parcel referencing is grounded in the INSPIRE Cadastral Parcels specification (SRC-004), which applies to European Union member states. Cadastral systems elsewhere differ in identifier structure, area authority and whether parcel geometry is legally definitive at all.

Campus benchmarking rules including the parent and child structure and the restricted list of campus-certifiable property types are US EPA ENERGY STAR rules (SRC-011) and do not generalise to other benchmarking schemes.

The physical access control pattern follows NIST SP 800-53 (SRC-007), a US federal control catalogue. Organisations operating under ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A or sector-specific regimes will map to equivalent but differently structured controls.
Coordinate reference systems, vertical datums and land-cover classifications are all jurisdiction-specific; the model requires that each be declared and never assumes a default.
Cadastral identifier schemes, title versus deeds systems, and whether government land is registered, are jurisdiction-specific.
INSPIRE ETRS89 practices apply in the EU; WGS84 approximate points are common in BIM and may be inappropriate for cadastral use.
CERCLA/RCRA overlays are United States law; other jurisdictions need local contaminated-land instruments.
Davis-Bacon site of the work is United States labour law; other public-works wage envelopes will differ.
Campus as an English operational term is common in ISO 19650-3 examples but is not a translated statutory class.
Common-law versus civil-law treatment of easements, superficie and condominium will change RRR cardinality.
adversarial_checks: Counterexample sought for site-facility separation: IFC 4.3 permits a facility to be aggregated directly by IfcProject without an intervening site (SRC-002), so a site is not universally required. The model therefore treats containment of a facility by a site as a recorded relationship with its own evidence rather than a structural necessity, and does not require every facility to have a parent site.

Counterexample sought for contiguity: EPA campus guidance and real portfolio practice both include discontiguous holdings managed as one unit. The managed-extent finding therefore makes contiguity an explicit recorded flag with a federation justification, rather than assuming a single connected polygon (SRC-011).

Attractive but unsupported structure rejected: a universal site typology (industrial, campus, port, depot and so on) was drafted and then rejected, because no reviewed primary source publishes a governed cross-domain site classification. Classification is instead modelled as scheme-versioned assignments with a precedence rule, and the absence of a canonical scheme is recorded in the checklist.

Attractive but unsupported structure rejected: a site-owned tenure and rights sub-model was drafted and removed. LADM (SRC-010) and INSPIRE (SRC-004) place rights, restrictions and responsibilities with the land administration domain, and IFC 4.3 deprecated its own land-title attribute (SRC-001). Duplicating it here would have created two competing sources of legal truth.

Boundary stress test between site and reporting view: because both EPA Portfolio Manager (SRC-011) and GHG Protocol (SRC-013) produce site-shaped boundaries that diverge from physical management, a policy was added forbidding a reporting boundary from redefining the managed extent. Without it an agent would silently corrupt the site definition when compiling a return.

Identity stress test: a date, a name, an address and a coordinate pair were each tested as identifier candidates and rejected. FRS demonstrates that names and addresses are exactly the attributes that fail to resolve duplicate site records across roughly ninety systems (SRC-003), which is why match confidence, not attribute equality, governs reconciliation.

Sourcing stress test: four intended sources could not be read live in this session (gs1.org and iso.org return HTTP 403, ecfr.gov redirects off-host, and the ENERGY STAR campus PDF is not machine-readable). Every claim that would have depended on GS1 GLN was removed rather than asserted from memory; ISO catalogue entries are cited for title, edition and scope only, never for clause-level text; and OSHA's own hosted text was used in place of eCFR.
A site can exist without a cadastral parcel (unregistered public land, water, informal occupation); requiring LandTitleID would falsely exclude those holdings.
A campus can be non-contiguous (satellite teaching hospitals, split data-centre halls); forcing a single polygon would corrupt identity.
A construction site of the work can exist with IsPermanentID=false and no land title; collapsing it into the permanent campus would break wage-law and safety records.
A company town can be both settlement and site; storing it only as WM-BLT-008 would hide populated-place semantics.
A logical ISA-95 site with no geometry must not satisfy canonical physical-site validation.
Multiple operators on one parcel (business park, hospital-plus-university) require many operator roles, not duplicate parcel identities.
Air-rights or subsurface campuses over railways would fail a 2D fence-line-only model.
A CERCLA plume extending off-site must not enlarge the managed campus identity.
Publishing full IfcSite geometry for a secure campus would violate ISO 19650-5 security-minded practice even if CityGML interoperability encourages it.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Base (claude) types WM-BLT-008 as an entity; grok types it as an aggregate. A site is a singular governed thing with its own identifier, lifecycle, duty holder, authorisations and record, and it can exist with a single facility or none at all, so aggregation is not constitutive. The COMPLEX / ELEMENT / PARTIAL composition that motivates grok's 'aggregate' reading is a recursive relationship between site instances plus a containment edge to WM-BLT-006, which the entity typing already carries. Typing the model as an aggregate would blur the boundary against the facility model and against reporting-boundary constructs that are also site-shaped collections. Entry kind accepted as entity; grok's composition semantics are absorbed as relationships and a composition function.

decisions.rationale: Claude states seven neighbour boundaries with explicit distinctions and source refs, separates managed extent from reporting boundary, legal parcel, settlement, utility network and asset-management system, and applies a consistent reference-not-re-model rule. Grok's in-scope list pulls rights, restrictions, responsibilities and planning controls inside while declaring the land-administration object out of scope, which is a less crisp edge. Size was not the deciding factor.

A site holds identity, lifecycle, duty holder and authorisations independent of what it contains, and can contain zero facilities. Composition is modelled as recursive site relationships plus containment edges, so aggregate typing would add no expressive power and would blur the WM-BLT-006 edge.

Base declares CRS and datum but omits the engineering-to-map conversion and the approximate-WGS84 caveat on IfcSite reference latitude and longitude, which is the dominant real-world georeferencing failure and is directly evidenced in IFC 4.3 and LandInfra.

Buildable area, coverage ratio, floor-area ratio and height limit are wholly absent from the base yet are core constraints on a managed land holding, evidenced by Pset_SiteCommon; planning authority is also distinguished from land owner, which the base never does.

decisions.concept: Construction site of the work as a time-bounded overlay
decisions.rationale: The base only has a phase flag on parts of a permanent site. A labour-law or construction envelope can be larger or smaller than the permanent holding and must not be collapsed into it; grok evidences this from 29 CFR 5.2 and IsPermanentID.

decisions.concept: Cadastral SpatialUnitGroup, informal tenure and strata fragmentation
decisions.disposition: rejected as a finding, deferred to research
decisions.rationale: Grok's cadastral-and-land-division-alignment overlaps the base's parcel-and-tenure-linkage on its primary question, and the genuinely novel parts (LADM SpatialUnitGroup grouping, unregistered or customary occupation, condominium and air-right fragmentation) sit on the land-administration side of the base's stated boundary. Deferred rather than duplicated.

A logical enterprise site with no land holding is an alignment target, not a canonical instance of a physical container. The base's standards-alignment-and-system-crosswalks finding already carries alignment targets, mapping loss and matching confidence, and grok itself records no distinctive artifact for this node.

decisions.disposition: rejected as a finding, deferred as a terminology hazard
decisions.rationale: Grok's contamination finding overlaps the base's hazard-exposure finding on contamination status and remediation. Its distinctive value is the warning that a statutory 'facility' is an environmental-liability object that must not be merged into WM-BLT-006; that belongs in boundary guidance and deferred research, and the responsible-party operation is captured by the added record-environmental-status function.

canonical-identifiers and names-and-postal-address restate the base's site-identity-and-designation (master identifier, governed global identifier, Dimension UUID, naming and retirement) and its address questions under external-context-and-connection-points. Land title identifiers remain referenced through the parcel linkage.

Base already asks composition type (complex, site, section), scheme-versioned classification and contiguity with a federation justification. Campus is retained as an operational alias in the scope statement rather than as a competing spatial primitive, consistent with ISO 19650-3 naming campuses without defining a feature type.

decisions.disposition: retained from base, unmatched by grok
decisions.rationale: The rule that an ENERGY STAR parent/child structure or a GHG Protocol organisational boundary may never redefine the managed extent is a load-bearing safeguard present only in the base; without it an agent would corrupt the site definition while compiling a return.

decisions.disposition: retained from base, unmatched by grok
decisions.rationale: SOSA phenomenon-time versus result-time separation grounds the model's temporal discipline for observations and has no counterpart in grok, which treats weather and observation as out of scope.

decisions.disposition: retained from base with regional flag
decisions.rationale: Written plan, evacuation, muster, accounting, alarm and review triggers come from US OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38 and are the only emergency structure either provider produced; the jurisdictional narrowness is carried as a publication hold, not a reason to drop the layer.

compute-site-quantities and publish-interop-mapping are covered by the base's validate-site-record, compile-reporting-boundary and reconcile-external-site-identifiers; the planned-versus-measured area distinction is absorbed into the base's existing quantities finding rather than a new operation.

Both providers place measurement, evidence and interoperability in a single terminal bundle with identical intent, so the service-layer structures are merged into the base's bundle rather than kept as parallel branches.

publicationHolds: Source and live-version verification is incomplete: the two providers cite IFC 4.3 from different hosts (ifc43-docs.standards.buildingsmart.org versus standards.buildingsmart.org) and different documentation builds, and grok-sourced Pset_SiteCommon, Pset_LandRegistration and IfcMapConversion claims must be re-fetched and pinned against the single host and version chosen for the base before merge.

Paywalled and blocked sources remain unverified at clause level: ISO catalogue entries (55001, 19650-1, 19650-3, 19152-1, 19152-2, 41011, 6707-1), IEC 62264-1 and the ENERGY STAR campus guide PDF were cited for title, edition and scope only; no clause-level wording may be published as quotation or requirement.

Multi-profile domain validation is not complete: the synthesised model must be exercised against at least three materially different site profiles (for example a university or hospital campus, a process or industrial site, and a port, data-centre or utility holding) before publication, since the evidence pack contains no instance-level validation.

Jurisdictional profile verification is outstanding: emergency planning (29 CFR 1910.38), regulatory site identity (EPA FRS), benchmarking (ENERGY STAR), physical security (NIST SP 800-53), contaminated land (CERCLA/RCRA) and construction wage envelopes (29 CFR 5.2) are all United States instruments; at least one non-US jurisdiction cross-check is required before the model is presented as jurisdiction-neutral.

No governed global location identifier scheme is asserted: GS1 GLN could not be fetched (HTTP 403) and ISO/IEC 81346 reference designation texts are paywalled, so any identifier-grammar claim must stay out of the published draft.
deferredResearch: LADM SpatialUnitGroup binding for multi-parcel campuses, plus unregistered, customary and informal occupation, and condominium, strata and air-right fragmentation: decide whether the site model needs an explicit binding pattern or remains a reference to the land-administration sibling model.

Terminology collision between the statutory CERCLA/RCRA 'facility' (any site or area where a hazardous substance has come to be located, or all contiguous land under common control) and the ISO 41011 facility used by WM-BLT-006: an explicit overlay rule is needed so environmental-liability objects are never merged into the facility model or allowed to enlarge the managed extent.

IEC 62264 / ISA-95 role-based site alignment: confirm that a geometry-less logical enterprise site is an alignment target only and cannot satisfy canonical physical-site validation, and record where the enterprise hierarchy is authoritative for rough-cut planning.

Marine, subsurface, offshore and relocatable managed holdings: neither provider located a primary source defining a managed-site container for these cases; the vertical-extent and water-body accommodations are partial and the boundary is unresolved.
Non-US contaminated-land and major-hazard regimes (Seveso, IED, UK COMAH and equivalents) as overlays on the hazard and authorisation structure, to test whether the US-derived structure generalises.
Site-level accessibility requirements and biodiversity or ecological baseline accounting: both appear only as single questions or constraints, with no primary standard cited by either provider.
