findings.name: Location fix and observation quality
findings.description: A dated statement of the item's whereabouts resolved against a place reference, distinguishing the point of observation from the business location asserted afterwards, and carrying precision and source.

findings.name: Containment and carrier context
findings.description: What the item was inside when observed: a handling unit, a vehicle, a room or another item, and how aggregation and disaggregation change that context without changing item identity.

layers.name: Custody, possession and rights
layers.description: Who physically holds the item and under what basis, kept strictly distinct from who owns it.

findings.name: Custody record and transfer
findings.description: Periods during which a named party held the item, the basis of holding, and the transfer events between holders, aligned with ISO 22095 custody terminology and EPCIS source/destination and shipping/receiving semantics.

findings.name: Ownership and rights reference
findings.description: The reference to legal title and encumbrances held in the ownership sibling model, and the rule that possession does not imply title. CIDOC CRM distinguishes current owner (P52) from keeper (P49); ISO 55000 frames value-bearing entities as assets of an organization.

bundles.name: Events, provenance and evidence
bundles.description: The event backbone that produces every other statement about the item, its time semantics, its origin story and the evidence that supports claims.
bundles.rationale: EPCIS models visibility as events answering what, when, where, why and how, with eventTime and recordTime distinguished; PROV-O models generation, derivation and attribution; W3C Verifiable Credentials supply issuer-signed evidence. Together they let claims about an item be traced and challenged rather than merely asserted.

layers.name: Event record and time semantics
layers.description: How events about the item are captured, corrected and ordered in time.

findings.name: Event capture and correction
findings.description: The event structure that records what happened to the item, why, where and how, and the rules for idempotent capture, correction and retraction of events that must not be silently overwritten.

findings.name: Time semantics and ordering
findings.description: The separation of when something happened from when it was recorded, the required timestamp form, and how ordering is decided when clocks disagree. RFC 3339 requires a stated offset to UTC, with 'Z' for zero offset and '-00:00' where the local offset is unknown; EPCIS carries eventTime, eventTimeZoneOffset and repository recordTime separately.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Time semantics govern fields carried by every other finding rather than producing a document of their own. The rules are inline constraints and reference data (offset handling, ordering, precision qualifiers); materialising them as an artifact would duplicate the event stream and the canonicalisation rules already recorded in the service layers.

findings.name: Event dimensions
findings.description: EPCIS 2.0 records What, When, Where, Why and How. Event types are ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransactionEvent, TransformationEvent and AssociationEvent. When includes event time and record time. Why includes bizStep, disposition and persistentDisposition. How includes sensor elements in 2.0. Instance EPCs must not be mixed up with class-level EPCs. Event hash identifiers and business-transaction hash URIs appear in CBV 2.0.

layers.name: Provenance and evidence
layers.description: Where the item came from, through whose hands, and what evidence supports each claim.

findings.name: Origin and chain of custody provenance
findings.description: The origin of the individual (maker, place, date of production or first observation) and the ordered chain of custody from origin to the present, including declared gaps. PROV-O supplies generation, derivation and attribution; ISO 22095 supplies the custody model vocabulary.

findings.name: Attestations, evidence quality and conflicting claims
findings.description: How each claim about the item is supported, who vouches for it, how strong that support is, and what happens when two credible sources disagree.

bundles.name: Record governance and interoperability
bundles.description: Who governs the item record, who may see what, how long it is kept, and how it exchanges with external standards without overclaiming conformance.
bundles.rationale: The record is not the thing. IEC 63278-1 frames a standardized digital representation of an asset across its lifecycle; PROV-O separates entities from the agents responsible for them; GDPR constrains item records that link to identifiable people; product-passport regimes impose external disclosure duties on the economic operator.

layers.name: Record stewardship, access and retention
layers.description: Mastership and authority over the record, scoped disclosure, and privacy and retention duties.

findings.name: Mastership, authority and record lifecycle
findings.description: Which system and which party master this record, who may assert or change each part of it, and how record versions relate to the physical thing they describe.

findings.name: Access scoping and disclosure views
findings.description: Which audiences may see which parts of the record, including a public identity view that deliberately withholds whereabouts and holder, and the exceptions that override the default.

findings.name: Privacy exposure and retention
findings.description: When item data becomes personal data, and how retention duties for traceability are reconciled with data-protection limits. GDPR applies to processing of personal data about identifiable natural persons; item records routinely carry holder identity, ownership history and movement traces.

layers.name: External alignment and exchange
layers.description: How this model maps to external standards and exchanges item data without asserting unproven conformance.

findings.name: Identifier and vocabulary alignment
findings.description: Mappings from this model's terms to external vocabularies (GS1 EPCIS/CBV, GS1 Digital Link, schema.org, IEC 63278-1, CIDOC CRM, PROV-O) recorded as alignments with known conflicts, never as conformance claims.

findings.name: Exchange projections and external obligations
findings.description: The outbound payloads built from this model (visibility events, product-passport content, credential presentations) and the obligations that attach when data is published to an external regime.

model.name: Gazetteer Place
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an AI agent needs to understand, create, inspect and operate a governed gazetteer place record: a named real-world location identified by a geographic identifier, with temporally scoped toponyms, classification, position, authority, provenance, relationships and access controls.
model.scope_statement: The model covers one place as recorded in a gazetteer, i.e. an ISO 19112 location instance identified by a geographic identifier within a declared location type and gazetteer register. It covers naming (multilingual, multi-script, temporally scoped), place-type classification, representative position and geometry with declared CRS and accuracy, existence and record lifecycle, naming authority and decisions, provenance and attestation, hierarchy and topology, cross-gazetteer concordance, sensitivity and access control, validation and retention. It excludes address semantics, coordinate reference system definition, boundary determination, cartographic rendering and any observation that merely cites a place.
in_scope: Place record identity, identifier minting, persistence and resolution
Toponyms with language, script, transliteration, pronunciation, nativeness, status and temporal validity
Place type / feature type classification including local types and type change over time
Representative position, geometry set, extent, CRS declaration and coordinate encoding constraints
Positional accuracy, resolution, viewing-scale bounds and fitness-for-use statements
Real-world existence period and record version lifespan, including uncertain and open-ended dates
Supersession, merge, split, deprecation and tombstoning of place records
Naming authority scope, official status, decision process and effective dates
Contested, disputed and competing names or claims and their audience-scoped presentation
Custodian, administrator, contributor, licence and editorial lineage
Partitive/administrative hierarchy and topological or associative relations to other places
Concordance to external gazetteers with match type and confidence
Sensitivity classification, locality generalization and access rules
Validation, conformance testing and quality measurement
Exchange encodings and query-service projections as non-semantic renderings
out_of_scope: Address and addressable-object semantics (ISO 19160-1 address model, address components, postal templates)
Definition of coordinate reference systems, datums and transformations (ISO 19111 / EPSG registry content)
Legal determination or delimitation of administrative and international boundaries
Cadastral parcels, property rights and land tenure
Building, facility and asset management records
Commercial point-of-interest operations such as opening hours, capacity, booking and pricing
Transport network topology, route segments and navigation instructions
Cartographic styling, symbolisation and map production
Observation, occurrence, event or transaction records that merely reference a place
Language, script, country and currency code registries themselves

boundary_notes.distinction: A gazetteer place is a named real-world feature referenced indirectly by a geographic identifier; an address is a structured, human-oriented designation of an addressable object. ISO/TC 211 concluded that addressing requirements are sufficiently different from the scope of ISO 19112, so address components must be referenced, not absorbed.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Administrative unit and statistical geography registers (UN M49, ISO 3166, INSPIRE AU)
boundary_notes.distinction: This model records that a place sits in, or is coded to, an administrative or statistical area and carries country codes; it does not define the area hierarchy, its legal basis or its boundary geometry, which remain owned by the register. UN M49 explicitly disclaims political interpretation of its groupings.

The place record declares which CRS its coordinates are expressed in and how they are encoded; the definition of the CRS, its datum and its transformations is external. GeoSPARQL 1.1 treats spatial reference system as a broader category than CRS and relies on external CRS identity in geometry literals.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Point-of-interest / local business model (schema.org Place and LocalBusiness)
boundary_notes.distinction: schema.org Place mixes stable physical extension with operational commerce attributes such as opening hours, capacity and booking pages. Only the stable named-place core is in scope; operational and commercial attributes belong to a sibling POI/venue model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Place type / feature type vocabulary (GeoNames feature classes and codes, Getty AAT, INSPIRE NamedPlaceTypeValue)
boundary_notes.distinction: The model requires a classification assertion with a resolvable vocabulary concept and optional source label, but the controlled vocabulary itself is a separate classifier model with its own versioning and deprecation rules.

Attestations, citations and name sources are first-class here as links plus temporal and confidence qualifiers, but the bibliographic description of the cited work (authors, edition, holdings) is delegated to a citation model.

functions.name: Mint place record
functions.description: Create a new governed place record for a location instance that no existing record covers, assigning identity per the identity priority.
inputs: candidate name assertions with language and script
evidence of distinctness from existing records
outputs: initial record version with begin lifespan timestamp
preconditions: Location type is defined and admits the candidate
A duplicate-detection search over names, type and extent returned no match above threshold
At least one attesting source is supplied
effects: Identifier is reserved permanently and may never be reused
Record enters the change log as version 1 with an RFC 3339 ingestion timestamp
Record is queued for validation before publication

functions.name: Resolve geographic identifier to position
functions.description: Resolve a geographic identifier, within a stated location type and gazetteer, to a representative position or extent — the indirect spatial referencing operation ISO 19112 exists to support.
outputs: representative position or extent in the requested CRS
preconditions: The identifier is current or a supersession chain can be followed
A geometry or representative point exists, or a containing place can be substituted
effects: Returns a tombstone with a successor pointer when the identifier is deprecated
Records the resolution in the access log when the record is sensitivity-restricted

functions.name: Assert or revise a name
functions.description: Add or revise a temporally scoped name assertion with language, script, transliteration scheme, status, nativeness and attesting citation.
outputs: name assertion attached to the place
updated preferred label if preference changed
preconditions: Script and language codes resolve in their registries
At least one citation or a record-level temporal scope is supplied
Naming authority scope is stated when the status is official
effects: Prior official name is closed with an end date rather than overwritten
Superseded names remain searchable but may be display-suppressed

functions.name: Record a naming decision
functions.description: Register a decision by a naming authority, its dossier, decision date and effective date, and apply the resulting official-name change.
preconditions: The authority's competence covers this place and feature class
Applicable naming policies have been assessed and recorded
effects: Official status transfers to the decided name from the effective date
Event time and ingestion time are recorded separately
Downstream consumers are notified through the change feed

functions.name: Assert geometry or representative position
functions.description: Attach a geometry or representative point with role, CRS declaration, certainty, temporal scope and citation, and set or revise the default geometry.
preconditions: CRS identifier resolves and axis order is declared
Geometry passes structural validity and antimeridian tests
Coordinate precision does not exceed justified accuracy
effects: Previous default geometry is retained and temporally closed
Positional accuracy and viewing-scale bounds are re-evaluated

functions.name: Classify place type
functions.description: Assign or revise place type assertions against a governed vocabulary, retaining source labels and distinguishing real-world change from correction.
outputs: crosswalk row when a source label is newly mapped
preconditions: The concept resolves in the declared vocabulary version
The type is admissible for the record's location type
effects: Coarse feature class is recomputed for reconciliation and filtering
Hierarchy admissibility constraints are re-checked

functions.name: Link external concordance
functions.description: Assert a typed link to an external gazetteer or authority record with match strength, method, confidence and evidence.
preconditions: The external target resolves and is not deprecated
Exact-match assertions are supported by explicit evidence
effects: Conflicting exact matches trigger downgrade review
Supersession of the external target schedules revalidation

functions.name: Supersede, merge or split records
functions.description: Execute an adjudicated succession between place records, maintaining supersedes and superseded_by chains and publishing tombstones.
outputs: updated succession pointers on all affected records
preconditions: An adjudication decision exists with named adjudicating role
All affected concordances have been enumerated
effects: Superseded identifiers remain resolvable and are never reused
Change feed entry is emitted for downstream consumers

functions.name: Apply sensitivity classification and generalization
functions.description: Assign a sensitivity category and produce a generalized public representation while retaining the precise value under controlled custody.
preconditions: The deciding party holds provider authority over the record
A retention location for the precise value is designated
effects: Public representations serve only the generalized value
Unredacted access requires authorisation and is logged
Category is re-examined at the recorded review date

functions.name: Validate place record
functions.description: Run structural, semantic and profile validation against declared schemas, shapes and constraints, and record the outcome.
inputs: schema and shape set with versions
preconditions: Mandatory element set for the profile is declared
Schema and shape versions are pinned
effects: Records failing mandatory rules are withheld from publication
Conformance claims are updated only where test evidence exists

functions.name: Project record to an encoding
functions.description: Render the format-neutral record into a target encoding or profile, declaring any information loss introduced by the projection.
preconditions: Target profile is registered and its loss profile is documented
Requested CRS is supported or the default is applied
effects: Semantics of the record are unchanged; only the rendering differs
Extensions are carried through documented namespaced mechanisms

functions.name: Query places by space, time and attribute
functions.description: Retrieve place records filtered by bounding box, temporal interval, type, name and hierarchy, with paging and link relations.
preconditions: Requester is entitled to the sensitivity tier of the matched records
Temporal filter syntax is valid, including open-ended intervals
effects: Sensitivity-restricted matches are returned generalized or omitted with disclosure
Access to restricted records is written to the audit log

functions.name: Deprecate and dispose
functions.description: Deprecate a record with a tombstone or dispose of retained material according to the retention schedule, without destroying identity or succession chains.
outputs: redaction markers where content was removed
preconditions: Retention period has elapsed or a lawful erasure basis is recorded
Successor or explanation is available for external citers
effects: Identifier remains reserved and resolvable
Disposal is recorded with an RFC 3339 timestamp and approving role

functions.name: Traverse parent-child hierarchy
functions.description: Follow preferred and additional parents or children, including historical and polyhierarchical paths.
preconditions: Place exists in the gazetteer
effects: Read-only navigation of location-instance links

functions.name: Reverse geocode position to candidate places
functions.description: Return named places whose position or extent contains or is near a point, filtered by feature type and viewing resolution.
preconditions: Point CRS is known or assumed WGS 84 as a finding CRS
effects: Read-only candidate set; proximity is not a hierarchical parent

functions.name: Propose a new name or name change
functions.description: Submit a names-authority proposal for an unnamed feature or a change to an existing official name, with local-usage evidence and compelling reason.
preconditions: Proposer meets the names-authority submission rules
Feature class is within the authority's purview
effects: Creates a proposal casefile; does not by itself change the standardized name

functions.name: Publish or transact a gazetteer item
functions.description: Insert, update or retire a location instance through a gazetteer service or register process, including ISO 19135-style item status.
preconditions: Custodian or editor role
Record satisfies the gazetteer schema and validation policies
effects: Creates or versions the register item; sets lifespan timestamps; may emit exchange encodings

composition.target: Gazetteer register and location type registry (ISO 19112 gazetteer / location type)
composition.purpose: Every place record must declare the gazetteer that publishes it and the location type whose definition it satisfies; the register and type definitions are governed separately from individual instances.

composition.target: Address and addressable-object model (ISO 19160-1 conceptual model)
composition.purpose: Link a place to addresses that designate it without importing address component or postal-template semantics, which ISO/TC 211 treats as a distinct scope from geographic identifiers.

composition.target: Country and area code registry (ISO 3166-1 and UN M49)
composition.purpose: Supply the country or area codes that contextualise the place; LPF makes country codes a required property and the register carries the disclaimer about legal status and frontiers.

composition.target: Administrative and statistical area model (INSPIRE Administrative Units, national admin hierarchies)
composition.purpose: Provide the parent administrative and statistical units that a place belongs to, without duplicating their legal basis, boundary geometry or versioning.

composition.target: Coordinate reference system model (ISO 19111 / EPSG-style register)
composition.purpose: Resolve the CRS identifiers declared on geometries and support transformation provenance; CRS definitions are external and must not be restated here.

composition.target: Language, script and transliteration registries (ISO 639, ISO 15924, romanization systems)
composition.purpose: Validate the language, script and transliteration-scheme values on every name spelling, as required by the INSPIRE GeographicalName structure.

composition.target: Place type vocabulary / feature classifier model (GeoNames feature codes, Getty AAT place types, INSPIRE code lists)
composition.purpose: Supply resolvable place-type concepts and their versioning and deprecation rules; the place record holds only the classification assertion and its source label.
Compose the place with zero or more geometries carrying role, CRS, temporal scope, certainty and serialisation, following the GeoSPARQL separation of feature from geometry.
Attach per-assertion citations with locus, date and confidence to names, types, geometries and relations, as LPF and INSPIRE sourceOfName require.

composition.target: Agent and organisation model (authorities, custodians, contributors)
composition.purpose: Identify naming authorities, gazetteer custodians, instance administrators and contributors as governed agents rather than free-text strings.

composition.target: Temporal period vocabulary model (named historical periods)
composition.purpose: Resolve named period concepts used to scope existence, names and geometries where calendar dates are unavailable or inappropriate.
Carry licence, attribution and inherited source restrictions on the record and on derived representations.
Alignment target for NamedPlace, GeographicalName, SpellingOfName and lifespan versioning; alignment is asserted at element level and does not by itself constitute a conformance claim.
Alignment target for temporally scoped names, types, geometries, relations and typed links, and for the required title, country codes and feature classes.

composition.target: OGC GeoSPARQL 1.1 Feature and Geometry ontology
composition.purpose: Alignment target for feature-geometry structure, serialisations and topological relation families when the record is projected to RDF.
Alignment target for the query-service projection: item addressing, bbox and datetime parameters, default CRS and link relations.

composition.target: Point-of-interest and venue model (schema.org Place / LocalBusiness operational attributes)
composition.purpose: Alignment for web discoverability of the stable named-place core while explicitly excluding operational and commercial attributes.

composition.target: Sensitive-data handling policy model (graded generalization and disclosure)
composition.purpose: Apply graded sensitivity categories, generalization magnitudes, disclosure fields and review dates to any place whose precise location can cause harm.

owner_package_requirements: Name a single accountable custodian for the gazetteer register and a named administrator role for each location type in scope, with a published contact and escalation path.
Declare the territory of use, the naming authorities recognised as competent within it, and the usage domains for which their decisions are treated as binding versus advisory.
Publish the licence, attribution requirement and any inherited source restrictions before redistributing toponymic data, and record the sensitivity policy and its decision owner.
Pin the versions of every external registry the package depends on (place type vocabulary, language and script registries, country codes, CRS register) and state the upgrade procedure.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint place URIs in a Dimension-controlled HTTPS namespace using opaque, non-semantic local identifiers, for example https://{dimension-host}/place/{ulid}, so that renaming, reclassification or re-delimitation never forces an identifier change. Never encode a name, coordinate, type or date in the identifier. Never reuse a retired local identifier. Where an authoritative master-system identifier exists, carry it as a governed alternative identifier with its scheme URI rather than adopting it as the local key, and keep external authority identifiers strictly in the concordance layer.
registry_links: Gazetteer register and location type registry maintained by the adopting Dimension (ISO 19112 conceptual schema)
Country and area code registry: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2/alpha-3 with UN M49 numeric codes and region groupings
Language and script registries: ISO 639 language codes and ISO 15924 script codes, plus the recognised romanization systems
Place type vocabulary register with version pinning and deprecation policy
Coordinate reference system register supplying CRS identifiers used in geometry declarations
External gazetteer concordance register recording target authorities, link types and revalidation cadence

canonicalization_rules: Normalise all toponym text to Unicode NFC and store the script code with every spelling; retain diacritics in the canonical form and generate folded variants only as derived search indexes.

Store coordinates in the declared CRS with an explicit axis-order statement; where a lon/lat geographic CRS is used, follow longitude-before-latitude decimal degrees and truncate precision to the justified accuracy.
Express every timestamp in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and keep event time, observation time and ingestion time in separate elements.
Serialise geometries canonically (fixed vertex order, closed rings, antimeridian-split parts) and record a digest of the canonical serialisation to detect silent geometry change.
Order multi-valued collections deterministically — names by status then language then script, types by preference then concept URI, links by link type then target URI — so that diffs are stable.
Represent absent knowledge with explicit reason codes or sentinel states rather than empty strings, null coordinates or a fabricated default parent.
patch_rules: Address patches to stable element identifiers, never to array positions, so that reordering does not corrupt a patch.

Distinguish a real-world change from a correction: a real-world change closes the prior assertion with an end date and adds a new temporally scoped assertion, while a correction supersedes the erroneous assertion and records the reason in the change log.
Never overwrite human-curated elements from an automated process; the controlled-field list must be checked before any bulk update and an override requires a named approving role.
Every patch records the asserting agent, the generation method, the event time and the ingestion timestamp; a patch without provenance is rejected.
Identifier, identifier scheme and succession pointers are append-or-close only; they are never rewritten in place.
A patch that would remove a mandatory element or an existing citation is rejected unless it is accompanied by a superseding assertion or an approved erasure decision.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional element, an additional encoding profile or a new code-list value is a minor, backward-compatible change.

Removing or making mandatory an existing element, changing identifier semantics, changing the default CRS or changing coordinate axis order is a breaking change requiring a major version and a migration note.
Code-list values are deprecated with a successor pointer and a sunset date rather than deleted; consumers must be able to interpret historical records containing retired values.
Alignment to an external standard may be asserted at element level at any time; a conformance claim may be published only when executed test evidence for a named conformance class exists.
Projections may add namespaced extensions but must not redefine the semantics of elements defined by the target encoding.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the place (for example a national gazetteer feature identifier or an INSPIRE external object identifier), carried with its scheme URI.
Governed global identifier or IRI — a persistent HTTPS URI in a namespace controlled by a recognised authority or by the adopting Dimension, resolvable and never reused.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only where neither of the above exists; a date, a name, a coordinate pair or a file path is never an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All artifact and record timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z. Event time (decision date, effective date, real-world change), observation or survey time, and ingestion or recording time are stored in separate elements and are never collapsed into one value; where only a date is known, a date value is used and is not silently widened to a timestamp.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named {register-code}-{artifact-kind}-{RFC 3339 UTC date}-{zero-padded sequence}, for example GAZ-validation-2026-08-24-003, with the sequence monotonically increasing within the date and never reused. Serials identify the artifact instance only; the subject place is referenced by its identifier, never by the serial.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every stored artifact carries a SHA-256 checksum of its canonical byte form and, for geometry artifacts, a separate digest of the canonical geometry serialisation. Decision dossiers, sensitivity assessments and release logs are append-only and, where the authority supports it, retain the signed original. Any artifact whose checksum cannot be reproduced is quarantined and reported rather than silently replaced.

policies: Identity is permanent: an identifier once issued is never reused, never repurposed and never deleted; removal is deprecation with a tombstone and, where applicable, a successor pointer.
Names are assertions, not facts: every name carries its language, script, status, nativeness, temporal validity and at least one attesting source or an explicit record-level temporal scope.
Officiality is scoped: no name is presented as official without naming the deciding authority, its territory of competence and the audiences for whom the decision is binding.

Dispute is data: competing names, claims and parentages are recorded as parallel assertions with their sources; the register does not silently adopt one side, and audience-scoped presentation is accompanied by a disclaimer that no position on legal status or boundary delimitation is implied.
Precision is not accuracy: recorded coordinate precision must not exceed documented positional accuracy, and any deliberate generalization must be disclosed in dedicated fields.

Harm review precedes publication: places whose precise location can endanger people, cultural property, sacred sites or threatened populations are assessed, categorised, generalized to the category's resolution and given a recorded review date.
Alignment is not conformance: external standards are recorded as alignments with element-level mappings; a conformance claim requires executed test evidence for a named conformance class.
Format neutrality: JSON, YAML, Markdown, GML, RDF, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of the record; no semantic element may be defined only in terms of one projection.
Standardized or official names take display precedence over compiled or crowd-sourced forms when a names authority has jurisdiction.
Historical, variant, pejorative and avoid-use names are retained with flags for retrieval and audit; they are not used for new indexing.
Indigenous, minority and local-use names are recorded with community or authority warrant and are not overwritten by exonyms.
Cave and other legally protected locations have coordinates withheld from public projections.
Addresses, postal codes, buildings-as-assets and CRS definitions are referenced, not stored as the gazetteer place.
Conformance to ISO 19112, INSPIRE GN or OGC WFS-G is claimed only with evidence; otherwise records are alignments.

read: Public reads return the current record version in the requested encoding with its licence, attribution, CRS declaration and any generalization disclosure.
Historical reads are supported by version and by valid-time: a caller may request the record as it was recorded at an ingestion timestamp, or as it was true at a real-world instant.
Requests for deprecated identifiers return a tombstone carrying the deprecation reason, timestamp and successor pointer rather than a not-found response.
Reads of sensitivity-restricted records return the generalized representation with disclosure fields unless the caller is authorised, and authorised reads are logged.
Bulk reads and change feeds expose version boundaries so that consumers can synchronise without re-fetching the whole register.
create: Creation requires a location type, a gazetteer register, at least one name assertion with language or an explicit undetermined value, a country or area code and at least one attesting source.
Duplicate detection over names, type and extent must be executed and its negative result recorded before an identifier is minted.
New records are validated against the pinned schema and shape set before publication; records failing mandatory rules are quarantined with a remediation owner.
Creation writes version 1 to the change log with begin lifespan version, asserting agent and generation method.
update: Real-world change closes the prior assertion with an end date and adds a new temporally scoped assertion; the identifier is unchanged.
Correction supersedes the erroneous assertion, records the reason and retains the superseded value in the change log.
Controlled, human-curated elements are protected from automated update unless an override is approved by a named role.
Changes to official status require a referenced naming decision with decision date and effective date.
Every update writes ingestion time separately from event time and recomputes the geometry digest where geometry changed.
delete: Hard deletion of a published place record is prohibited; deprecation with a tombstone is the standard removal.
Merge, split, absorption, rescope and retraction are executed only through an adjudicated succession decision that enumerates all affected identifiers and concordances.
Lawful erasure removes only the specific elements under obligation, leaves a redaction marker, and preserves the identifier, the succession chain and the audit trail.
Disposal of retained versions, logs and evidence follows the published retention schedule and is recorded in the disposal register with an approving role and an RFC 3339 timestamp.

roles.name: Gazetteer Custodian
responsibilities: Hold accountability for the register's scope, territory of use, licence and publication commitments
Approve location type definitions and profile version changes
Own the retention schedule and approve disposals

roles.name: Toponymic Editor
responsibilities: Create and revise name assertions with language, script, status, nativeness and attestation
Adjudicate conflicting name evidence and record the basis
Maintain preferred-label selection rules and display suppression of retained variants

roles.name: Naming Authority Liaison
responsibilities: Track the competence and mandates of recognised naming authorities
Lodge, monitor and record naming proposals, dossiers, decisions and effective dates
Escalate contested names and maintain the contested place register

roles.name: Spatial Data Steward
responsibilities: Assert and maintain geometries, CRS declarations and representative positions
Evaluate and publish positional accuracy and viewing-scale bounds
Investigate topology anomalies such as same-type overlaps and hierarchy geometry inconsistencies

roles.name: Sensitivity and Access Officer
responsibilities: Assign and review sensitivity categories and generalization magnitudes
Authorise and log releases of unredacted representations
Own erasure decisions and redaction markers

roles.name: Interoperability Engineer
responsibilities: Maintain encoding profiles, projection loss declarations and the service definition
Operate validation and conformance test runs and publish reports
Maintain concordances, match confidence and revalidation on external supersession

access.default_rule: Place records are open by default under the declared licence, served at the resolution permitted by their sensitivity category; access to unredacted positions, evidence dossiers, decision case files and access logs is restricted to named roles and is logged.
exceptions: Sensitivity-restricted places: public callers receive only the generalized representation plus disclosure fields; unredacted access requires an approved agreement and a named authorising role.

Contested naming material: draft adjudications and internal deliberation notes in the contested place register are withheld until the adjudication is closed, while the competing assertions themselves remain public.
Embargoed naming decisions: a decision dossier may be withheld until the authority publishes it, with the embargo end date recorded.
Third-party licensed source material inside evidence dossiers may be non-redistributable even where the place record is open; the dossier is then served as citation metadata only.
Personal data incidentally present in notes or contributor records is restricted regardless of the openness of the place record.
Authorised researchers or land-management agents may receive withheld cave or other protected coordinates under an auditable exception.
Indigenous-name records may have community-specified access tighter than the gazetteer default.
Internal compiled dumps may include licence-restricted sources that cannot be redistributed.
audit_requirements: Every read of an unredacted sensitivity-restricted record logs requester identity, authorising role, purpose, returned resolution and an RFC 3339 timestamp.
Every write logs the asserting agent, generation method, event time, ingestion time and the changed element paths.
Every succession, deprecation, erasure and disposal action logs the approving role, the reason and all affected identifiers.
Access logs are append-only, retained under the retention schedule independently of the records they describe, and reviewed on a stated cadence.
Log identifier resolution of restricted records, all official-name decisions, merges, disclosure-class changes and access exceptions with RFC 3339 timestamps and actor identity.

read_order: AGENTS.md — establish the model name, type, and the specification, storage, interface and process entry points before touching any data
Specification URL — read the scope, exclusions and boundary notes, and confirm the subject is a gazetteer place and not an address, administrative unit or POI
Storage type URL — learn the projection in use (document store, graph, files under version control) and the canonicalisation rules that apply to it
Interface URL — learn the query and write contract, supported encodings, CRS handling and paging before issuing any request
Processes URL — read the naming decision, succession, sensitivity and retention procedures before creating, updating or removing any record
Registry links — resolve pinned versions of place type, language, script, country and CRS registries before validating or asserting values

coverage.claim: Covers the governed decision and operating surface of a gazetteer place record — identity and indirect referencing, multilingual temporally scoped naming, classification, position, accuracy and CRS declaration, real-world existence versus record lifecycle, naming authority and dispute, custodianship, assertion-level provenance, hierarchy and topology, cross-gazetteer concordance, sensitivity, validation and retention — grounded in ISO 19112 (concept level only), INSPIRE Geographical Names, OGC GeoSPARQL and OGC API - Features, W3C/OGC SDW best practices, IETF GeoJSON, UNGEGN, US BGN/GNIS, UN M49 and the Linked Places, GeoNames, Who's On First, Getty TGN and GBIF bodies of practice, extended by three grok-sourced findings for gazetteer-as-register item status, administrative-versus-physical facet, and deprecated/derogatory/community-restricted name governance. Not claimed complete for any specific national gazetteer, for NGA GNS-governed non-US official names, for marine, undersea or extraterrestrial naming regimes, for Indigenous data-sovereignty instruments, or for jurisdictions whose naming law was not examined.

checklist.notes: Identifier priority, opaque persistent identifiers, HTTPS URI minting, non-reuse, alternative geographic identifiers and duplicate adjudication are specified and grounded in ISO 19112, GNIS Feature ID practice, Who's On First wof:id and the SDW persistent-URI best practice.

Record version lifespan, change classification, supersession, merge, split, deprecation, tombstoning and disposal are separated from real-world existence, grounded in INSPIRE lifespan versioning, Who's On First supersedes/superseded_by and Getty TGN merge and deletion rules.

Partitive and administrative hierarchy with multiple concurrent schemes and explicit unknown/contested parentage, formal topological relation families, associative relations and typed external links are all covered from GeoSPARQL, LPF, GeoNames, Who's On First and schema.org.

Real-world existence, name validity, type and geometry validity and record time are kept on separate clocks; open-ended and approximate intervals, named periods and certainty are supported per LPF, with RFC 3339 required for machine timestamps.

Assertion-level citation rather than record-level attribution, evidence kind, contributor, editorial control and machine-versus-human generation are covered from INSPIRE sourceOfName, LPF per-element citations, Getty TGN sources and contributors and Who's On First controlled fields.
Custodian, instance administrator, contributor, licence and inherited source restrictions are explicit, with named accountable roles and a required owner package for the adopting Dimension.

Structural, shape-based and semantic validation with pinned schema versions, mandatory element sets, publishability gating and the distinction between alignment and evidenced conformance are covered from GeoSPARQL SHACL shapes, INSPIRE validation practice, LPF required properties and the SDW validation best practice.

Default openness with graded sensitivity restriction, audience-scoped presentation for contested names, embargoes, third-party licence limits and comprehensive audit requirements are specified from GBIF sensitive-data practice and SDW responsible-use guidance.
Prohibition on hard deletion and identifier reuse, tombstones with successor pointers, retention classes, lawful partial erasure with redaction markers and a disposal register are specified.

Encoding profiles, declared projection loss, extension mechanisms, service contract with bbox/datetime/limit and link relations, CRS negotiation, and concordance link strength with revalidation are covered from RFC 7946, OGC API - Features, GeoSPARQL, INSPIRE GML and LPF.

Language, script, transliteration scheme, pronunciation, nativeness, status, preference and display suppression follow the INSPIRE GeographicalName and SpellingOfName structure and UNGEGN romanization concerns.

Governed place-type concepts with source labels, coarse feature classes, preferred type, multiplicity rules, temporal scoping and a crosswalk artifact are covered from INSPIRE, LPF fclasses, GeoNames feature classes and codes, and Getty TGN preferred place type.

Representative point, multiple roled geometries, null geometry with reason, CRS declaration and axis order, transformation provenance, antimeridian handling, positional accuracy and viewing-scale bounds are covered.

Bounded officiality, delegated competence, decision dossiers with docket, policy basis, consultation, decision and effective dates, and reconsideration paths are grounded in US BGN principles and policies and UNGEGN's national standardisation mandate.

Positional accuracy with method and confidence, published quality measures for completeness, currency and duplicate rate, and match confidence on concordances are all represented as measured rather than asserted values.

Graded generalization, withholding disclosure, provider-held decision authority and review dates are covered from GBIF practice, which addresses species localities. Indigenous and culturally restricted place-name governance — including community consent, restricted-knowledge protocols and traditional-knowledge labelling — is represented only generically; no Indigenous data governance instrument was examined in this pass, so this node is marked a gap rather than presented as canonical.

Restriction of critical-infrastructure and security-sensitive locations is handled by the same graded sensitivity mechanism, but no national security classification regime was consulted, so mapping between sensitivity categories and government classification levels is undefined.

known_omissions: ISO 19112:2019 clause-level attribute names could not be verified against the normative text in this session: the ISO catalogue page returned HTTP 403 and the preview PDF was not machine-readable. Concept-level claims (gazetteer, location instance, location type, geographic identifier, custodian, administrator, territory of use) are grounded in ISO catalogue metadata and corroborating open sources; exact attribute names, cardinalities and any 2019 renaming relative to the 2003 edition are unverified.

The revision date of the US BGN Principles, Policies, and Procedures could not be extracted because the hosted PDF was not machine-readable; the policy content cited (presumption against changing established names, commemorative-name restrictions, prohibition on derogatory names) is corroborated but the exact edition is unstated.

Extended Date/Time Format (ISO 8601-2 levels) was intended as the grounding for uncertain and approximate dates but the Library of Congress specification pages returned HTTP 403; temporal uncertainty is therefore grounded in the LPF 'when' object alone, and the specific EDTF syntax for uncertainty, approximation and unspecified digits is not asserted.

Maritime, undersea and extraterrestrial naming regimes (IHO undersea feature names, IAU planetary nomenclature) were not examined; the model may need additional authority and classification structure for those domains.

Postal, statistical and electoral geographies that reuse place names with different extents are treated only through hierarchy schemes; no dedicated finding covers the reconciliation of name-sharing units with divergent boundaries.
Multilingual sorting and collation for display and indexing is acknowledged in canonicalisation but no collation authority was examined.
No treatment of crowd-sourced contribution moderation, vandalism detection or trust scoring, despite UNGEGN noting crowd-sourced geographic information as a working-group concern.

Full ISO 19112:2019 UML attribute list is paywalled; 2019 class names (Location, LocationClass, Gazetteer, GeographicIdentifier) are taken from the official abstract, TC 211 requirement and publicly quoted edition-2 change list, while 2003 SI_* properties are evidenced by OGC 11-122r1.
NGA GNS field dictionary (UFI/UNI, name type, designation) was not retrieved; non-US official names often depend on that register and remain a gap.
IHO SCUFN undersea feature names, IAU WGPSN extraterrestrial names, and World Historical Gazetteer / Linked Places Format / Pelagios are not primary-sourced here.
Indigenous data-sovereignty protocols (CARE Principles, UNDRIP applied to toponyms) are only indirectly covered via UNGEGN promotion of indigenous names.
ADL Gazetteer Content Standard and Feature Type Thesaurus are historically important but were not fetched as live first-party schema in this run.
ISO 19155 Place Identifier architecture and GeoSPARQL geometry semantics are not modelled beyond complementary geometry.
National gazetteers beyond GNIS/INSPIRE/GeoNames/TGN (for example Ordnance Survey Open Names, Canadian Geographical Names) are acknowledged as sources to GeoNames rather than fully modelled.
conflicts: Identifier form differs across authorities: GNIS uses a numeric ANSI-standard Feature ID, INSPIRE uses a namespace-plus-localId external object identifier, Who's On First uses an externally minted integer, and the SDW best practices call for HTTP URIs. The model resolves this by keeping the master-system identifier as a governed alternative identifier and minting a separate opaque local key and URI, but a single register cannot satisfy all four native forms simultaneously.

GeoJSON fixes the CRS to WGS 84 with longitude-before-latitude and forbids alternative CRS declarations, while OGC API - Features and GeoSPARQL support other CRSs; a record served as plain GeoJSON therefore cannot faithfully carry a non-WGS 84 geometry and must declare that projection loss.

Plain GeoJSON has no native slot for temporally scoped names, types or geometries; LPF resolves this with JSON-LD foreign members, but a consumer treating LPF as ordinary GeoJSON will silently see only one name and one geometry.

Officiality conflicts across authorities: a name official for one government's use is not binding on others, and the same feature may carry different official names under different states. UN M49 explicitly disclaims any position on legal status, so a register that presents a single official name is making an editorial choice rather than reporting a fact.

Preferred-parent modelling differs: Getty TGN designates one preferred parent with non-preferred alternatives, while Who's On First permits sentinel states for unknown, complicated, contested or multiple parentage. Forcing TGN-style single preference onto contested places produces false assertions.

GBIF-style generalization improves safety but degrades positional accuracy and can break topological containment checks; the accuracy statement and the generalization statement can therefore appear to contradict one another unless both are published.
ISO 19112:2019 optional/descriptive position versus INSPIRE NamedPlace required geometry.
ISO 19112:2019 Location/Gazetteer class names versus OGC 11-122r1 use of ISO 19112:2003 SI_LocationInstance.
OGC 11-122r1 is a Best Practice, not an OGC Standard; OGC now points implementers to OGC API Features.
Feature-type schemes conflict: INSPIRE NamedPlaceTypeValue, GeoNames 9 classes/645 codes, GNIS ~43 retrieval classes with no official generic-term definitions, TGN AAT-linked place types.
GNIS 2021 removal of most cultural feature classes versus GeoNames and TGN retention of many man-made or inhabited-place types.
GeoNames wiki edits versus UNGEGN/BGN names-authority sanction.
TGN approximate finding coordinates versus GIS-grade geometry.
INSPIRE does not rank competing official endonyms; UNGEGN prefers a single official spelling per feature where possible.
regional_assumptions: Naming authority structure is modelled on regimes with an identifiable national or federal names board and delegated sub-national authorities, exemplified by the US BGN and by UNGEGN's national standardisation framework. Jurisdictions with no statutory names authority, or with competing sub-national authorities, will need locally defined precedence rules.
The country-code context assumes ISO 3166-1 and UN M49 apply; places in territories with contested or absent code assignments require the contested-claims mechanism rather than a code value.

INSPIRE-derived elements (lifespan versioning, viewing-scale bounds, nativeness, name status) reflect European regulatory practice and are treated as a strong alignment rather than a universal requirement.

US-specific policies such as the commemorative-name waiting period and the single-official-name-per-feature rule are cited as evidence that such policies exist and must be modelled, not as globally applicable rules.

Sensitivity categories are drawn from a biodiversity context; thresholds expressed in decimal degrees behave differently at high latitudes and may be inappropriate for cultural or security sensitivity in other regions.
WGS 84 is assumed as the de facto finding CRS for complementary points (GeoNames, TGN, typical GNIS decimal degrees), not as a universal legal CRS.
U.S. BGN/GNIS rules, including cave-location withholding and cultural-feature exclusions, apply to U.S. domestic names and must not be globalised.
INSPIRE NamedPlace obligations apply to European spatial-data infrastructure exchange, not to all gazetteers.
UNGEGN romanization keys and endonym preference apply where a national names authority exists; many territories have none.
English-language preferred-name practice in TGN legacy data is an editorial convention, not a global rule.
NGA GNS remains the usual non-US official compiled source even though its field dictionary was not fetched.
adversarial_checks: Attempted to justify a bundle for 'address and postal delivery' inside this model and rejected it: ISO/TC 211's own review concluded that addressing requirements are sufficiently different from the scope of ISO 19112, so addresses are a referenced sibling rather than a layer here.

Attempted to justify operational attributes (opening hours, capacity, booking, accessibility) because schema.org Place carries them, and rejected them: they describe a venue's operation, not a named place's identity, and admitting them would collapse the boundary with a POI model.

Searched for a counterexample to 'one place, one name' and found several: GNIS permits exactly one official name for Federal use while retaining variants, Getty TGN requires preferred plus vernacular and historical names, and INSPIRE permits multiple GeographicalNames each with multiple spellings. The model therefore treats names as a set of scoped assertions with a derived preferred label, not as a scalar field.

Tested whether geometry can be treated as mandatory and found it cannot: LPF explicitly permits a null geometry and Getty TGN records places known only by hierarchy, so geometry is optional with a required absence reason and a fallback to indirect referencing through a containing place.

Tested whether a date can serve as an identifier or as a version key and rejected it: decision date, effective date and ingestion timestamp routinely diverge, and several records can share a date, so identity is opaque and versions are sequenced independently of dates.

Tested whether 'conformance' to ISO 19112, INSPIRE or GeoSPARQL could be claimed from element-level similarity and rejected it: no conformance test evidence was executed in this research, so every external standard is recorded as an alignment and the compatibility rules forbid promoting an alignment to a conformance claim without test evidence.

Tested whether hard deletion could ever be correct for an erroneous record and rejected it as the default: external systems cite gazetteer identifiers, so retraction is modelled as supersession with a tombstone, with partial erasure reserved for lawful obligations and always leaving a redaction marker.
Could an address, postal code or cadastral parcel be smuggled in as a gazetteer place? ISO 19112 sends addressing to ISO 19160-1; GNIS explicitly excludes ZIP Codes; those remain sibling models.
Could a date, centroid or preferred-name string be used as identity? The identity priority forbids it; merges require former-id maps rather than renaming the key to a date.
Could community GeoNames edits be treated as BGN or UNGEGN official names? Policy requires authority-sanctioned versus compiled flags.
Could withheld cave coordinates leak through nearby, dump or reverse-geocode functions? Restrict-sensitive-location and access exceptions exist specifically to prevent that.

Could ISO 19112:2019 conformance be claimed from OGC 11-122r1 or from INSPIRE GN alone? Conflicts and Best Practice status are recorded; conformance requires evidence against the 2019 gazetteer conformance class.
Could fictional or legendary places enter via historical-lost handling? TGN excludes legendary places; location-certainty and historical warrant questions force that distinction.
Could feature-type crosswalks silently equate mountain, peak and populated place across schemes? Type scheme is mandatory and crosswalk is an alignment with mapping notes.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently converge on entity, and the referent is a persistent, separately identifiable thing — an ISO 19112 location instance carrying a geographic identifier that survives renaming, reclassification and geometry revision — rather than an event, process or classifier. The boundary is complete on both sides: address semantics are delegated to ISO 19160-1 on ISO/TC 211's own reasoning, CRS and datum definition to ISO 19111/EPSG, legal boundary delimitation and cadastre to administrative-unit siblings, operational commerce attributes to a POI/venue sibling, and place-type vocabularies to a classifier model. No split is warranted: the toponym is a scoped assertion set on the place, not an independently governed entry, and the gazetteer register itself is admitted only as membership context, not as a co-equal node.

decisions.rationale: Not chosen for size. Claude's boundary is the more complete on both sides: an explicit out-of-scope enumeration, six boundary notes each carrying source refs, and the ISO/TC 211 reasoning for delegating addressing to ISO 19160-1. It also closes governance surfaces grok leaves open — retention and tombstoning, validation and conformance-versus-alignment, and CRS declaration and encoding constraints — and keeps real-world time, name validity time and record time on separate clocks.

Providers agree, and the referent satisfies the entity test: an opaque persistent identifier survives renaming, reclassification and re-delimitation, and both providers independently reject a date, a coordinate pair or a preferred-name string as identity.

ISO 19112 assigns addressing to ISO 19160-1 and ISO/TC 211 concluded addressing requirements differ sufficiently from ISO 19112's scope. Both providers reached this independently and GNIS explicitly excludes ZIP Codes; admitting address components would collapse two distinct spatial-reference systems.

decisions.concept: Coordinate reference system and datum definition
decisions.rationale: The place record declares which CRS its coordinates are expressed in and how they are encoded; ISO 19111 and the EPSG register own the definition, datum and transformation content. Retained in base as a declaration and provenance obligation only.

schema.org Place mixes stable physical extension with opening hours, capacity and booking. The base adversarial check correctly refuses them: they describe a venue's operation rather than a named place's identity, and admitting them dissolves the boundary with a POI model.

decisions.concept: Gazetteer as ISO 19135-1 register with item status
decisions.rationale: Materially missing from base, which governs dataset version lifespan but not register item status, territory of use, or membership of one place in several gazetteers. Evidenced by the retrievable ISO/TC 211 requirement identifier rather than by paywalled text alone.

decisions.concept: Administrative versus physical facet and gazetteer class scope
decisions.rationale: Orthogonal to the base type/local-type/multiplicity finding, and carries the boundary-crossing parent placement rule plus the in-scope-or-sibling decision that GNIS's 2021 cultural-class removal makes unavoidable.

decisions.concept: Deprecated, derogatory and community-restricted name forms
decisions.rationale: Partially fills a gap the base itself declares. TGN's retain-but-flag treatment of pejorative and avoid-use names, and the community or authority warrant for indigenous and minority names, operate on the name form and are not covered by base status/nativeness qualifiers or by coordinate generalization.

decisions.concept: Preferred name, variants, homographs and per-name term identifiers
decisions.disposition: Rejected as duplicative; two elements deferred
decisions.rationale: The finding's centre of gravity — preferred name and variant set — is already carried by two base findings. Homograph disambiguation via parent string or qualifier, and a persistent term identifier per name form distinct from the place identifier, are genuine base omissions but belong folded into existing base findings rather than added as a third overlapping naming node.

decisions.concept: Complementary coordinates, point convention and elevation
decisions.rationale: Base representative-position and CRS-declaration findings already cover geometry role, default geometry selection, null geometry with reason, certainty and encoding. Elevation and the centroid-versus-mouth-versus-source convention are increments inside an already-covered finding, not a missing one.

decisions.disposition: Rejected as duplicative; operation accepted instead
decisions.rationale: Base partitive-and-administrative-hierarchy already models multiple concurrent hierarchies, preferred parents and sentinel unknown/contested parentage. What was actually missing was the traversal operation, which is accepted as a function.

decisions.concept: Source warrant, contributor and quality finding
decisions.rationale: Base source-attestation finding is the stronger statement of the same content: it enforces assertion-level rather than record-level citation and additionally distinguishes machine-generated from human-verified assertions.

decisions.concept: Restricted disclosure, licence and retention finding
decisions.disposition: Rejected as duplicative; statutory suppression deferred
decisions.rationale: Base splits this content across sensitivity/generalization, custodianship/licence and retention/tombstoning findings, each more developed. The specific mode of withholding a feature's very existence under the Federal Cave Resources Protection Act and 43 CFR Part 37 is a distinct disclosure mode and is deferred rather than dropped.

decisions.disposition: Rejected as normative; retained as historical alignment
decisions.rationale: Grok itself records that 11-122r1 is an OGC Best Practice and not a Standard, and that OGC API - Features is the successor family. Base already specifies the OGC API - Features contract with collections/items paths, bbox, datetime, limit and link relations, so the base contract governs.

decisions.concept: Legendary and fictional places excluded; lost and planned-but-unbuilt places included
decisions.rationale: Grok's TGN-evidenced edge is a real refinement of the base scope statement, which is silent on it, but it changes scope prose rather than adding a node. Recorded so the synthesizer does not silently adopt it and so it can be confirmed against primary text before publication.

decisions.disposition: Base terminology retained; discrepancy escalated to publication hold
decisions.rationale: Claude uses location type and location instance; grok reports 2019 class names Location, LocationClass, Gazetteer and GeographicIdentifier. Neither provider reached the normative text, so this is unverified vocabulary rather than a substantive contradiction and must not be resolved by adjudication.

publicationHolds: ISO 19112:2019 normative text was reached by neither provider (ISO catalogue returned HTTP 403 for one, paywalled for the other). Class names, attribute names, cardinalities and the 2003-to-2019 rename set are unverified, and the two providers report different vocabularies for the same construct. Verify against the purchased standard or the ISO/TC 211 register before publishing any wording that a reader could mistake for a conformance statement.

Live-URL and version-pin verification for every accepted source. Specifically: the US BGN Principles, Policies and Procedures edition date was not machine-extractable; the INSPIRE Geographical Names Technical Guidelines are cited by the two providers as a versioned PDF (v3.1.0, 2024-07-31) and as a knowledge-base landing page and must be reconciled to one pinned artifact; and the three grok-sourced additions carry only tier-2 or accessed-page evidence.

Multi-profile domain validation is incomplete. The model is exercised only against US BGN/GNIS, INSPIRE/EU regulatory practice and compiled gazetteers (GeoNames, Getty TGN, Who's On First, Linked Places Format). Run it against at least one non-US, non-EU national names authority and one historical or linked-pasts gazetteer profile before publication, and re-test the ISO 19112 descriptive-position case against INSPIRE's mandatory NamedPlace geometry to confirm the optional-geometry-with-absence-reason resolution holds in both profiles.

Indigenous and culturally restricted place-name governance is a gap the base declares and the accepted grok finding only partially fills. No Indigenous data-sovereignty instrument (CARE Principles, UNDRIP as applied to toponyms) was examined by either provider. Do not present the sensitivity and access layer as canonical, and mark the community-warrant question as provisional.

Temporal-uncertainty syntax is ungrounded: the intended EDTF (ISO 8601-2) grounding failed with HTTP 403, leaving approximate, uncertain and unspecified-digit dates supported only by the Linked Places 'when' object. Publish no specific uncertainty syntax.

Sensitivity categories and their thresholds derive from a biodiversity-occurrence context expressed in decimal degrees, and no national security-classification regime was consulted, so the mapping from sensitivity category to government classification level is undefined and the thresholds are unvalidated at high latitudes and for cultural restriction.
deferredResearch: NGA GNS field dictionary (UFI/UNI, name type, designation code) — neither provider retrieved it, and it is the usual governing register for non-US official names, so the officiality and identifier findings currently rest on US and EU practice alone.

IHO SCUFN undersea feature names and IAU WGPSN planetary nomenclature: both providers exclude marine, undersea and extraterrestrial naming regimes, which may require additional authority and classification structure.

Homograph disambiguation (parent string, qualifier, noted-homograph flag) and a persistent term identifier per name form distinct from the place identifier — to be folded into the base toponymy findings rather than added as a duplicate node.

INSPIRE relatedSpatialObject-style cross-theme linking: how a place record points at the same real-world entity held in a declared sibling model (administrative unit, built work, transport network) without collapsing the two, which the base boundary notes presuppose but no base finding governs.

Statutory suppression of a feature's very existence, as distinct from coordinate generalization — evidenced for caves by the Federal Cave Resources Protection Act and 43 CFR Part 37 — including how it must be enforced across nearby, reverse-geocode and bulk-dump paths.
ISO 19155 Place Identifier architecture, unmodelled by both providers, and its relationship to the identifier priority and concordance findings.
ADL Gazetteer Content Standard and Feature Type Thesaurus, and the UNGEGN Resolution 4 minimum digital-exchange set (name, feature type, location) as a candidate normative publishability floor.

Boundary edge confirmation for legendary and fictional places excluded versus lost, planned-but-unbuilt and archaeologically attested places included, plus multilingual collation authority and crowd-sourced contribution moderation, vandalism detection and trust scoring, all of which both providers list as untreated.

bundles.name: Place Identity and Naming
bundles.description: What the place is, how it is identified persistently, and how it is named across languages, scripts, statuses and time.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19112 makes the geographic identifier the referencing mechanism, while INSPIRE, GeoNames, Getty TGN and LPF all separate the stable place object from a set of temporally and linguistically qualified name assertions. Conflating identity with a name string is the single most common failure in gazetteer data.

layers.name: Identity and Identifiers
layers.description: Establishing and resolving the durable identity of the place record and its position in a gazetteer register.

findings.name: Place record identity and identifier minting
findings.description: A gazetteer place is identified by a persistent, opaque identifier that survives renaming, reclassification and geometry revision. Authoritative master-system identifiers (GNIS Feature ID, INSPIRE inspireId, national gazetteer key) take precedence; a governed HTTP URI is minted for web resolution; only where no external authority exists does the adopting Dimension mint a UUID or ULID. A date, a name or a coordinate pair is never the identifier.

findings.name: Geographic identifier, location type and indirect spatial referencing
findings.description: ISO 19112 positions a gazetteer as a directory of geographic identifiers describing location instances, where a location type defines the semantics of the instances it admits. The place record must therefore declare which gazetteer register and which location type it belongs to, and must support indirect referencing — resolving a label or code to a position rather than carrying coordinates alone.

findings.name: Gazetteer membership and register item
findings.description: ISO 19112:2019 defines a gazetteer as a register of location instances of one or more location sub-types containing some information regarding position, and recognises the gazetteer as a sub-type of ISO 19135-1 Register, with Location a RegisterItem. OGC WFS-G exposes gazetteer metadata and location instances over a feature service. A place may appear in more than one gazetteer.

layers.name: Toponymy and Multilingual Naming
layers.description: Name assertions attached to the place: their written forms, scripts, transliteration, pronunciation, status, nativeness and preference.

findings.name: Toponym form, language, script and transliteration
findings.description: A name is not a string: INSPIRE models GeographicalName with language, and one or more SpellingOfName each carrying text, ISO 15924 script and an optional transliteration scheme, plus optional PronunciationOfName with IPA and a sound link. Romanized forms must be traceable to the romanization system used, which is a standing UNGEGN concern.

findings.name: Name status, nativeness and preference
findings.description: Names carry a status (official, standardised, historical, variant) and a nativeness (endonym or exonym), and exactly one preferred label is normally selected per audience. GNIS permits only one official name per feature for Federal use with variants retained; Getty TGN requires a preferred name plus vernacular and historical variants; GeoNames types names as official, short, colloquial or historical.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Name status, nativeness and preference are qualifiers on inline name assertions within the place record. They generate no separate deliverable; the evidence that justifies a status is carried by the naming-decision artifact and the attestation artifact in other findings, which are referenced rather than duplicated here.

findings.name: Historical, deprecated and sensitive names
findings.description: TGN retains historical, misspelled, pejorative and avoid-use names for retrieval of legacy materials and flags them so they are not used for new indexing. GNIS marks obsolete names and vanished features as historical without implying age. GeoNames records historical and colloquial alternate-name types. These forms remain in the name set rather than being deleted.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Sensitivity and historical flags are inline attributes of name forms. Deletion is not used; restriction of display is a policy overlay rather than a separate artifact.

layers.name: Place Type Classification
layers.description: Assigning and governing the feature or place type of the place, including local types and type change over time.

findings.name: Feature type, local type and classification change
findings.description: Every governed place carries at least one type drawn from a resolvable vocabulary. INSPIRE separates a coarse NamedPlaceTypeValue from a free localType; LPF requires broad fclasses (A, H, L, P, R, S, T) plus optional vocabulary-typed types with source labels; GeoNames uses featureClass plus featureCode; Getty TGN requires a preferred place type. Types are temporally scoped because a village can become a suburb.

findings.name: Administrative versus physical facet
findings.description: TGN distinguishes Administrative records (inhabited places, nations, empires) from Physical records (mountains, rivers, oceans) and discourages a Both flag. Physical features that cross political boundaries are placed under the next containing hierarchical level. GNIS after 2021 focuses on natural features, unincorporated populated places and selected hydrographic and reservoir classes, and removed most cultural classes.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Facet and boundary-crossing flags are classification attributes of the place record rather than independent artifacts.

bundles.name: Spatial Footprint and Spatial Reference
bundles.description: Where the place is: representative position, geometry set, coordinate reference declaration, encoding constraints, accuracy and resolution.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19112 states that a gazetteer carries position information for each location instance; GeoSPARQL separates feature from geometry and allows several geometries with one default; RFC 7946 fixes a CRS and coordinate order; and the SDW best practices require explicit statements of coordinate encoding and positional accuracy. These are separable, independently governed concerns.

layers.name: Positioning and Geometry
layers.description: Representative point, geometry set, geometry roles and the encoding of coordinate values.

findings.name: Representative position and multiple geometries
findings.description: A place may carry a representative point, a bounding box, one or more detailed geometries, or no geometry at all. GeoSPARQL distinguishes hasGeometry from hasDefaultGeometry and provides derived centroid and area; LPF permits several temporally scoped geometries with per-geometry certainty and citations, or a null geometry; Getty TGN records point and bounding-box coordinates.

findings.name: CRS declaration and coordinate encoding constraints
findings.description: Coordinates are meaningless without a declared spatial reference. RFC 7946 fixes GeoJSON to WGS 84 with longitude before latitude; OGC API - Features defaults to OGC:CRS84 and requires explicit CRS negotiation for alternatives; GeoSPARQL carries CRS identity inside geometry literals; the SDW best practices require publishers to state how coordinate values are encoded and to choose a CRS suited to users.
findings.inline_only_rationale: CRS declaration and encoding rules are metadata carried alongside every geometry and every service response; they are reference data pointing into an external CRS register rather than a deliverable this model produces. The governing statement is published once in the dataset metadata artifact defined under custodianship.

layers.name: Spatial Reference Quality
layers.description: How good, how precise and at what scale the recorded position may legitimately be used.

findings.name: Positional accuracy, resolution and viewing-scale bounds
findings.description: The SDW best practices require describing positional accuracy and providing geometries at an appropriate level of accuracy, precision and size; INSPIRE NamedPlace carries mostDetailedViewingScale and leastDetailedViewingScale to bound legitimate display. Precision of coordinates must never be read as accuracy, and generalized coordinates must be labelled as such.

bundles.name: Temporal Existence and Record Lifecycle
bundles.description: When the place existed, when its names and attributes were valid, and how the record itself is versioned, superseded, merged, split or deprecated.
bundles.rationale: Real-world time and record time are different clocks. LPF scopes names, types, geometries and relations with a 'when' object supporting fuzzy and open-ended dates; INSPIRE carries beginLifespanVersion and endLifespanVersion for the record version; Who's On First carries supersedes/superseded_by and a last-modified stamp. Confusing the two clocks corrupts every historical query.

layers.name: Place Existence and Real-World Change
layers.description: The existence of the place in the world and the validity of its name assertions over time, including uncertainty.

findings.name: Existence period and temporal uncertainty
findings.description: Places begin, change and cease. LPF expresses temporal scope as timespans with start and end, each expressible as 'in', 'earliest' or 'latest', plus named periods, duration, label and certainty; GNIS marks features as historical when they no longer exist. The model must accept open, approximate and disjoint existence intervals without forcing a false precise date.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Existence periods are inline temporal qualifiers on the place and on each scoped assertion. The documentary evidence for a start or cessation date is held by the attestation artifact under evidence and lineage, and the period vocabulary is an external reference model; creating a separate temporal artifact here would duplicate both.

findings.name: Name validity periods and renaming events
findings.description: Names have their own validity independent of the place. Getty TGN records display dates with start and end dates on names; GeoNames types historicalName separately; GNIS records a BGN decision date. A renaming is an event with a decision, an effective date and a superseded prior official name that must remain searchable.

layers.name: Record Versioning and Succession
